rationale_c2: Radiomic feature extraction (PyRadiomics, ICC-filtered) from T2WI/ADC/DCE is an appropriate, standardized approach.
rationale_c3: Clear inclusion/exclusion criteria with well-documented patient flow across both institutions.
rationale_c4: Multivariable logistic regression combined Rad-score with PSAD and other clinical variables via backward stepwise selection.
rationale_c5: MRI acquisition and radiomic pipeline applied consistently, with SMOTE augmentation explicitly restricted to model development (not the external validation set).
criteria_note: MMAT v2018 quantitative non-randomized (2-institution retrospective, independent external validation cohort, SMOTE-augmented radiomics).
probast_rationale: Genuine independent external institutional validation is a relative strength, but 2,553 candidate radiomic features reduced via ANOVA/LASSO plus SMOTE class-balancing before model training carries substantial overfitting/optimism risk typical of this corpus.

title: Deep Learning with Quantitative Features of Magnetic Resonance Images to Predict Biochemical Recurrence of Radical Prostatectomy: A Multi-Center Study.
rationale_c1: Three-institution Beijing cohort (primary n=368, two validation cohorts n=34 and n=83), reasonably diverse but still a convenience, single-city sample.
rationale_c2: T2WI radiomic feature extraction (Pyradiomics) with pathology-registered tumor annotation is appropriate.
rationale_c3: Clear inclusion/exclusion criteria and complete outcome ascertainment (BCR by consecutive PSA readings) across cohorts.
rationale_c4: Clinical prognostic models (CAPRA-S, NCCN, GG-RP) compared against DRS-BCR via Cox regression, and pre/post-operative clinical variables adjusted in CS-combine model.
rationale_c5: MRI acquisition and radiomic/deep-learning pipeline applied consistently across the primary and two external validation cohorts.
criteria_note: MMAT v2018 quantitative non-randomized (multi-center retrospective, deep survival neural network, 2 external validation cohorts).
probast_rationale: Multi-center external validation (VC1 n=34, VC2 n=83) is a strength, but VC1 is very small, and the deep survival neural network was built from 155/702 pre-filtered radiomic features with a complex non-linear architecture, carrying meaningful overfitting risk despite dropout/early-stopping mitigation.

title: An integrated nomogram combining deep learning, Prostate Imaging-Reporting and Data System (PI-RADS) scoring, and clinical variables for identification of clinically significant prostate cancer on biparametric MRI: a retrospective multicentre study.
rationale_c1: Large multicentre retrospective cohort from five institutions across the USA and the Netherlands (n=592), among the most representative designs in this batch.
rationale_c2: MRI acquisition varied by site (endorectal vs pelvic phased-array coil) and PI-RADS scoring is subject to inter-reader variability, introducing some measurement heterogeneity.
rationale_c3: Clear inclusion/exclusion criteria and complete outcome data (GGG) across training and validation cohorts.
rationale_c4: Multivariable logistic regression (ClaD) explicitly adjusts for deep-learning score, PI-RADS and clinical variables (PSA, prostate volume, lesion volume).
rationale_c5: Deep learning pipeline, PI-RADS scoring, and clinical variable capture applied consistently across the training and independent validation sites.
criteria_note: MMAT v2018 quantitative non-randomized (5-site multicentre retrospective cohort, independent 2-site external validation, deep learning + clinical nomogram).
probast_rationale: The strongest-designed study in this batch: large multi-site cohort with a genuinely independent 2-site external validation, DeLong testing, decision-curve analysis, and comparison against an established risk calculator (PBCG). Residual concerns are inter-reader PI-RADS variability, mixed biopsy/prostatectomy ground truth (verification bias risk), and regularised logistic regression combining a deep-learning score with PI-RADS and clinical variables (moderate analytic complexity), none individually rising to clearly 'high' but collectively precluding an overall 'low' judgment.
appraisal_note: Best-reported study of this batch (Lancet Digit Health): public GitHub code repository, genuine external multicentre validation, and comparison against a clinical risk calculator (PBCG). PROBAST overall judged 'unclear' rather than 'low' given inter-reader PI-RADS variability and mixed biopsy/prostatectomy reference standards; this is a borderline call worth noting.

title: A Genomic-Clinicopathologic Nomogram for the Prediction of Lymph Node Invasion in Prostate Cancer.
rationale_c1: Single-source TCGA cohort (n=426) with no independent external institutional cohort for the nomogram; a small in-house RNA-seq set (n=5 matched pairs) validated only individual gene expression, not the full model.
rationale_c2: RNA-sequence expression quantification (FPKM) is an appropriate, standard measurement approach.
rationale_c3: Complete outcome data (lymph node status) for all 426 patients; class imbalance addressed methodologically via SMOTE.
rationale_c4: Multivariate logistic regression combined the SVM-based risk score with Gleason grade, with VIF-checked collinearity.
rationale_c5: RNA-seq and machine-learning pipeline applied consistently as intended.
criteria_note: MMAT v2018 quantitative non-randomized (single-source TCGA cohort, internal SMOTE-balanced train/validation split, no independent external cohort).
probast_rationale: No independent external validation cohort; the internal 'validation set' is an SMOTE-balanced split of the same single-source TCGA dataset, and synthetic minority oversampling applied prior to model development carries risk of optimistic performance estimates; 40 candidate genes were reduced via mRMR/SVM-RFE/LASSO with limited real (non-synthetic) LNI events (79).
appraisal_note: Borderline validation judgment: SMOTE-balanced 'validation set' is drawn from the same single TCGA source rather than an independent cohort; authors themselves note lack of external multicentre validation as a limitation.

title: Advanced Imaging Analysis in Prostate MRI: Building a Radiomic Signature to Predict Tumor Aggressiveness.
rationale_c1: Single tertiary-center retrospective cohort of biopsy-proven PCa undergoing prostatectomy; representativeness of the broader PCa population is unclear.
rationale_c2: MRI acquisition and radiomic feature extraction followed a standardized, reproducibility-tested pipeline (stability rank, single scanner).
rationale_c3: 40 of 102 patients (39%) were excluded for insufficient lesion volume, leaving only 62 for analysis, a substantial and selective attrition.
rationale_c4: No clinical confounders (age, PSA, comorbidities) were incorporated into the radiomic prediction models.
rationale_c5: Imaging protocol and segmentation approach were applied consistently across the analyzed cohort.
criteria_note: MMAT v2018 quantitative non-randomized (single-center radiomics signature, SVM classification with internal resampling).
probast_rationale: Substantial exclusion (39%) threatens participant selection; no independent validation set, only internal 10x undersampling resampling, raising overfitting concern typical of small radiomics signatures.
appraisal_note: Exploratory single-center study (n=62 analyzed after exclusion); no external validation cohort, only internal resampling; accuracy/sensitivity/specificity reported instead of AUC for most signatures.

title: A Nomogram Based on a Multiparametric Ultrasound Radiomics Model for Discrimination Between Malignant and Benign Prostate Lesions.
rationale_c1: Single-center retrospective cohort (n=112) with defined inclusion/exclusion criteria; generalizability beyond this population is uncertain.
rationale_c2: Ultrasound (B-mode/SWE) radiomics extraction was standardized with reported good intra-/inter-observer ICC.
rationale_c3: All 112 enrolled patients were accounted for with clear patient-flow reporting.
rationale_c4: Clinical confounders (age, PSAD) were identified via multivariate logistic regression and integrated into the combined nomogram.
rationale_c5: Imaging acquisition and biopsy protocol were applied consistently to all patients.
criteria_note: MMAT v2018 quantitative non-randomized (single-center radiomics nomogram with five-fold cross-validation).
probast_rationale: Single-center small cohort (n=112) with massive feature reduction (1218 to 20 features) via LASSO and only five-fold cross-validation, no external validation set, raising overfitting risk.

title: Identification of a Transcriptomic Prognostic Signature by Machine Learning Using a Combination of Small Cohorts of Prostate Cancer.
rationale_c1: Cohort combines three small, heterogeneous public/institutional RNA-seq datasets (n=52, 96, 23), limiting representativeness of any single population.
rationale_c2: RNA-seq processing followed a uniform, reproducible pipeline (Kallisto, RUVseq normalization) across all datasets.
rationale_c3: Patients with follow-up under 60 months and no BCR were excluded, which is methodologically justified but introduces potential selection bias.
rationale_c4: Omics-only, clinical-only, and combined models were compared, addressing clinico-pathological confounding.
rationale_c5: The machine-learning pipeline (feature selection, RF, hyperparameter tuning) was applied consistently across cohorts.
criteria_note: MMAT v2018 quantitative non-randomized (pooled small public/institutional RNA-seq cohorts, random forest signature).
probast_rationale: Small heterogeneous combined cohorts (total n=171, one arm n=23) with BCR follow-up-dependent case definition and leave-one-cohort-out validation; feature selection from 400 candidate genes down to 3 raises overfitting concern.
appraisal_note: Very small VPCC arm (n=23, 5 BCR events) is a notable applicability/precision concern despite overall low applicability concern rating.

title: Immune-Related Gene-Based Novel Subtypes to Establish a Model Predicting the Risk of Prostate Cancer.
rationale_c1: TCGA discovery cohort (n=487) validated in four independent public cohorts (GEO, cBioPortal, ICGC) spans varied populations and settings.
rationale_c2: Measurement platforms differ across validation cohorts (RNA-seq vs. microarray), introducing cross-platform comparability concerns.
rationale_c3: Patient flow and exclusions (incomplete clinical data) were clearly reported for the 487 analyzed patients.
rationale_c4: Multivariate Cox regression adjusted for age at diagnosis and pathological stage alongside the risk score.
rationale_c5: Consensus clustering and LASSO Cox model-building pipeline were applied uniformly across datasets.
criteria_note: MMAT v2018 quantitative non-randomized (TCGA discovery + 4 independent external validation cohorts, LASSO Cox risk model).
probast_rationale: Massive multi-step feature reduction (2976 DEGs to 263 immune DEGs to 896 to 104 to 6 genes via LASSO) is typical high-risk omics signature analysis, despite four external validation cohorts partially mitigating concern.

title: Development of a Novel, Multi-Parametric, MRI-Based Radiomic Nomogram for Differentiating Between Clinically Significant and Insignificant Prostate Cancer.
rationale_c1: Two-center consecutively enrolled cohort (n=159) with training, internal validation, and external validation groups improves representativeness.
rationale_c2: Radiomic feature extraction had high intra-/inter-observer ICC (0.78-0.93) supporting measurement reliability.
rationale_c3: SMOTE synthetic oversampling was used to address marked class imbalance (csPCa vs. ciPCa), complicating a straightforward completeness assessment.
rationale_c4: Multivariable logistic regression incorporated ADC value and PSA as independent clinical predictors.
rationale_c5: MRI acquisition and segmentation protocols were applied consistently within each center.
criteria_note: MMAT v2018 quantitative non-randomized (2-center radiomic nomogram, training/internal/external validation).
probast_rationale: Small and imbalanced training set (41 csPCa vs 13 ciPCa) with SMOTE oversampling and 1188-feature reduction via mRMR/LASSO raises analysis-domain risk despite external validation.

title: Radiomics Based on Multiparametric Magnetic Resonance Imaging to Predict Extraprostatic Extension of Prostate Cancer.
rationale_c1: Single-center retrospective cohort (95 patients/115 lesions), a limitation explicitly acknowledged by the authors.
rationale_c2: Radiomic feature extraction had good mean ICC (0.801) and blinded segmentation/pathology review.
rationale_c3: Patient/lesion flow with exclusion criteria was clearly reported (2 excluded for pathology, 14 for prior therapy/timing).
rationale_c4: A clinical model incorporating t-PSA and Gleason group was compared against and combined with the radiomics model.
rationale_c5: Same scanner/protocol and blinded segmentation were applied consistently across all lesions.
criteria_note: MMAT v2018 quantitative non-randomized (single-center radiomics + clinical nomogram, internal train/validation split).
probast_rationale: Single-center study with no external validation and an extreme feature-to-sample ratio (4580 features from 82 training lesions reduced via mRMR/LASSO to 8), a high analysis-domain risk explicitly acknowledged as a limitation by the authors.
appraisal_note: Authors explicitly note lack of external validation and single-scanner limitation.

title: Multi-omics Biomarker Pipeline Reveals Elevated Levels of Protein-glutamine Gamma-glutamyltransferase 4 in Seminal Plasma of Prostate Cancer Patients.
rationale_c1: Multi-center (3 sites) case/negative-biopsy referral cohort; representativeness of the broader screening population is uncertain.
rationale_c2: Rigorous tiered SRM/ELISA quantitative proteomics assay development with extensive QC is well described.
rationale_c3: Sample sizes and outcomes per phase (qualification, verification n=219, ELISA validation) are clearly reported.
rationale_c4: Age and serum PSA were used as covariates in multi-marker models, but broader clinical confounding (comorbidities, inflammation) was not addressed.
rationale_c5: Standardized sample collection/processing and assay protocols were applied consistently.
criteria_note: MMAT v2018 quantitative non-randomized (multi-tier SRM/ELISA biomarker discovery-verification with XGBoost multi-marker modeling).
probast_rationale: An exhaustive combinatorial search of 35,442 marker combinations with 10x10 cross-validation carries substantial overfitting/multiple-testing risk; final single-marker (TGM4) diagnostic AUC was modest (0.66).
appraisal_note: Borderline applies_prediction_appraisal call: primarily a discovery/verification proteomics pipeline, but includes explicit ML-based multi-marker predictive modeling with AUC/sensitivity/specificity, so scored yes per calibration default.

title: Temporal Stability and Prognostic Biomarker Potential of the Prostate Cancer Urine miRNA Transcriptome.
rationale_c1: Three independent cohorts (discovery n=10, training n=99, validation n=40) with active surveillance patients support representativeness for the risk-stratification question.
rationale_c2: NanoString nCounter miRNA profiling used a systematically optimized normalization pipeline.
rationale_c3: Patient numbers and outcomes are clearly reported for all three cohorts.
rationale_c4: The random forest model used only miRNA features; clinical confounders were not incorporated into the final predictive model.
rationale_c5: Urine collection and profiling protocol were applied consistently across cohorts.
criteria_note: MMAT v2018 quantitative non-randomized (discovery/training/independent validation cohorts, random forest urine miRNA biomarker).
probast_rationale: Independent validation cohort is small (n=40, 11 high-risk) with wide confidence intervals (AUC 0.74, 95% CI 0.55-0.92), and feature selection (7 miRNAs) was cross-validated but not externally replicated in a larger cohort.

title: Tissue Phenomics for prognostic biomarker discovery in low- and intermediate-risk prostate cancer.
rationale_c1: Single cohort of 90 low-/intermediate-risk post-prostatectomy patients; generalizability to broader PCa risk spectrum is uncertain.
rationale_c2: Highly detailed, standardized multiplex IHC/image-analysis (Tissue Phenomics) workflow with quality control is described.
rationale_c3: All 90 patients and 40 recurrence events are accounted for with clear cohort characteristics.
rationale_c4: Standard clinical variables (Gleason, stage, PSA, age) were shown not predictive but were not formally adjusted for in the final phene-based models.
rationale_c5: IHC staining, imaging, and phene-discovery pipeline were applied consistently to all cases.
criteria_note: MMAT v2018 quantitative non-randomized (single-cohort exploratory image-based phenomics biomarker discovery, methodology-focused paper).
probast_rationale: Small single-cohort (n=90) with a highly data-driven, iterative phene-discovery process (not prespecified) and comparison of multiple ML algorithms without clear external validation; reported accuracies (83-88%) lack confidence intervals or independent test set.
appraisal_note: Primarily a methodology/proof-of-concept paper describing the Tissue Phenomics discovery workflow; final predictive model specifics and validation strategy are not fully detailed in the available text, borderline for applies_prediction_appraisal (scored yes given reported recurrence-prediction accuracies).

title: Seminal plasma as a source of prostate cancer peptide biomarker candidates for detection of indolent and advanced disease.
rationale_c1: Multi-center open-label case/control study (n=125) with 4 disease groups; small subgroup sizes limit representativeness.
rationale_c2: CE-MS proteomic profiling with pre-analytical stability and analytical precision testing is rigorously described.
rationale_c3: Discovery and test set sample numbers per group are clearly reported with no unexplained loss.
rationale_c4: Control groups (chronic prostatitis, healthy controls) were significantly younger than PCa/BPH groups, an imbalance not adjusted for in the SVM models.
rationale_c5: Sample collection and CE-MS profiling protocol were applied consistently across sites.
criteria_note: MMAT v2018 quantitative non-randomized (multi-center case/control seminal plasma proteomics, SVM biomarker panels with discovery/test split).
probast_rationale: Small, age-imbalanced groups and a pronounced drop in classifier performance from training (AUC ~100%/99%) to independent test set (AUC 75%/83%) indicate substantial overfitting risk typical of small SVM biomarker panels.

title: Cancer genetics-guided discovery of serum biomarker signatures for diagnosis and prognosis of prostate cancer.
journal: Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A
rationale_c1: Single-institution human serum cohort (n=143) following a Pten-knockout mouse-guided candidate selection strategy; direct generalizability to unselected patients is uncertain.
rationale_c2: Targeted SRM/ELISA quantification of candidate glycoproteins is rigorously validated with external standards.
rationale_c3: Patient numbers at each analytic stage (FISH, SRM, ELISA, test set) are clearly reported.
rationale_c4: Candidate biomarkers were correlated with CRP and leukocyte counts to exclude confounding by inflammatory status.
rationale_c5: Serum collection and proteomic quantification protocols were applied consistently.
criteria_note: MMAT v2018 quantitative non-randomized (mouse-model-guided two-stage human serum biomarker discovery/verification with independent test set).
probast_rationale: Exhaustive screening of 21,699 regression models with bootstrap validation carries high overfitting risk, though partially mitigated by an independent test set for the diagnostic signature.

title: Pentachlorophenol enhances bladder cancer cell invasion through altered protein stability.
rationale_c1: TCGA-BLCA plus T24/SW780 lines match PCP invasion and mechanism aims.
rationale_c2: Invasion assays, RNA-seq, and survival ML use standard measurable endpoints.
rationale_c3: Clinical cohorts lack PCP exposure so PCPRS cannot represent exposure-linked prognosis.
rationale_c4: Prognostic score built with extensive ML screening; limited clinical confounder adjustment.
rationale_c5: Multi-cohort OS validation reported but moderate C-index and underpowered GSE5287.
criteria_note: MMAT v2018 quantitative non-randomized (public cohort + in vitro).
probast_rationale: Convenience TCGA/GEO samples without PCP data; 101-algorithm selection and training-set median cutoff risk overfitting.
appraisal_note: Borderline: PCPRS prognostic model applies PROBAST though decoupled from PCP exposure in patients.

title: Epigenomics-Guided Multi-Omics Integration Uncovers a Lipid-Metabolic Signature with Translational Utility in Bladder Cancer.
rationale_c1: TCGA discovery cohort plus four independent external cohorts (metastatic, NMIBC, MIBC, BCG-treated) span diverse BLCA settings, but platform heterogeneity across cohorts creates some uncertainty.
rationale_c2: Genome-wide DNA methylation and RNA-seq were integrated using a validated algorithm (MethylMix) with concordance testing.
rationale_c3: Sample sizes and outcomes are reported for the discovery and all four validation cohorts.
rationale_c4: Multivariate Cox regression adjusted for age, pathological stage, and molecular subtypes (TP53/FGFR2-3 mutation status).
rationale_c5: The integrative multi-omics and machine-learning pipeline was applied consistently across discovery and validation cohorts.
criteria_note: MMAT v2018 quantitative non-randomized (TCGA discovery + 4 independent external validation cohorts, random forest-derived 25-gene signature with in vitro functional validation).
probast_rationale: Large-scale feature reduction (494 concordant genes to 25-gene signature via random forest) is a high analysis-domain risk typical of omics signatures, despite validation across 4 independent external cohorts and outcome definitions (OS/DFS/RFS) that vary by cohort.
appraisal_note: Bladder cancer (not prostate) but within AIBIO_GU genitourinary oncology scope; journal-dated 2026 (accepted/published within the review's stated timeframe), included with no other flags.

title: Centrosome-related gene SPHK1 drives bladder cancer progression and therapeutic vulnerability.
rationale_c1: Convenience public cohorts (TCGA, GSE13507, GSE48075, IMvigor210) plus a self-constructed IHC cohort (n=56) with sampling method not fully specified, so representativeness of the target BLCA population is unclear.
rationale_c2: Expression, IHC, RT-qPCR and functional assays used standard, appropriately described methods.
rationale_c3: Survival outcome data appear complete for the analyzed cohorts with clear risk stratification.
rationale_c4: Multivariate Cox regression adjusted for age and pathological stage alongside the signature.
rationale_c5: Public omics data and wet-lab assays were applied per standard protocols as intended.
criteria_note: MMAT v2018 quantitative non-randomized (public cohorts + ML signature + experimental validation).
probast_rationale: 12-gene CRSS derived via LASSO/multiple ML algorithms with massive feature/algorithm selection typical of omics signatures; external validation present (GSE13507, IMvigor210) with modest AUCs (0.62-0.74).
appraisal_note: Combines prognostic signature (CRSS, nomogram, AUC 0.62-0.74) with mechanistic SPHK1 functional validation; appraised as predictive-model paper per calibration default.

title: A machine learning-guided epithelial plasticity score refines prognostication and immune-context stratification in muscle-invasive bladder cancer.
rationale_c1: Cohort is a convenience sample of TCGA-MIBC plus GEO/IMvigor210 cohorts across platforms; representativeness of a defined target population is unclear.
rationale_c2: Gene expression, WGCNA and consensus clustering measurements are standard and well described.
rationale_c3: Survival data essentially complete (368/366 patients) with explicit complete-case handling for the nomogram.
rationale_c4: Multivariable Cox and interaction testing adjusted for clinicopathological covariates and mRNA subtype.
rationale_c5: Ridge model projection into external cohorts followed pre-specified fixed-coefficient methodology.
criteria_note: MMAT v2018 quantitative non-randomized (public cohorts + 10-strategy ML model selection).
probast_rationale: EPRS built via candidate-gene expansion within the same training cohort then model selection across 10 algorithms; despite strong external validation (GSE32894, GSE13507, IMvigor210, GSE176307) and benchmarking against 6 published signatures, feature/algorithm selection risk remains high per corpus norm.
appraisal_note: One of the more methodologically rigorous papers in the batch (extensive multi-cohort external validation, head-to-head comparison with published signatures, formal interaction testing).

title: Non-invasive evaluation of muscle invasion and survival prognosis in bladder cancer using enhanced CT-based deep learning radiomics: a multi-center real-world cohort study.
rationale_c1: Consecutive real-world patients from 6 academic centers with explicit inclusion/exclusion criteria and a prospective 100-patient reader-study cohort.
rationale_c2: Imaging acquisition, segmentation (multi-reader consensus) and radiomic/DL feature extraction are rigorously described.
rationale_c3: Completeness of survival follow-up for the OS nomogram subset is not fully detailed, and marked cross-cohort heterogeneity (e.g., TCGA-BLCA AUC collapse to 0.519) suggests data/case-mix gaps.
rationale_c4: Multivariable Cox regression incorporated DLRN score alongside clinicopathological covariates.
rationale_c5: CT acquisition and AI-assisted reading were performed per pre-specified protocol including a counterbalanced crossover reader design.
criteria_note: MMAT v2018 quantitative non-randomized (multi-center real-world cohort, internal/external validation, embedded prospective human-AI reader study).
probast_rationale: DLRN combines 1834 radiomic features with 2048 ResNet101 features reduced via multi-step selection; external multi-center AUC (0.783) and internal AUC (0.807) are good, but marked domain shift in TCGA-BLCA cohort (AUC 0.519) signals analysis/generalizability risk typical of this corpus.
appraisal_note: Strongest study design in this batch: large multi-center real-world cohort (n=1370), internal+external validation, and a prospective human-AI reader study (12 readers) with de Long testing; notable performance collapse in the North American TCGA subset flags generalizability/domain-shift concern.

title: Radiogenomic analysis of muscle-invasive bladder cancer using CT-based texture analysis.
rationale_c1: Single small pilot cohort (n=89) from TCGA/TCIA with no external validation, explicitly acknowledged by authors as a study limitation restricting representativeness/generalizability.
rationale_c2: Radiomic feature extraction used a previously validated robust/reproducible (RRR) texture pipeline with manual expert segmentation.
rationale_c3: Nearly 50% of the cohort lacked distant metastasis information, explicitly noted by authors as limiting outcome completeness.
rationale_c4: Statistical comparison of the 89-patient subset vs. the full 412-patient TCGA cohort found no significant demographic/outcome differences.
rationale_c5: Imaging protocol and 10-fold cross-validation with SMOTE were applied consistently as pre-specified.
criteria_note: MMAT v2018 quantitative non-randomized (single small pilot cohort, no external validation).
probast_rationale: 488 texture features vs. n=89 with only internal 10-fold CV and no external validation; authors explicitly flag overfitting risk given the low events-per-feature ratio typical of small radiogenomic pilots.
appraisal_note: Authors explicitly self-identify as an unvalidated single-cohort pilot study with acknowledged overfitting risk; weakest internal validity in this batch.

title: Machine learning-based determination of sex-related bladder cancer biomarkers.
rationale_c1: Merged convenience samples from TCGA, GTEx and GEO (GSE133624) with z-score/ComBat-seq harmonization; representativeness of a defined clinical population is unclear.
rationale_c2: RNA-seq normalization (TPM, log2, z-score) and 5-fold cross-validated feature selection are standard and well documented.
rationale_c3: Complete transcriptomic and clinical (gender, stage) data were used per stratified subset.
rationale_c4: Batch/dataset was modeled as a covariate in DESeq2 to reduce confounding by cohort of origin.
rationale_c5: Cross-validation and normalization protocols were applied consistently as pre-specified.
criteria_note: MMAT v2018 quantitative non-randomized (merged public transcriptomic cohorts, 4-method ML feature selection with external validation).
probast_rationale: Aggregated panels (RRA across 4 feature-selection methods x 5 folds) evaluated on 2 small external GEO datasets (n=58, n=70) with bootstrap CIs; strong AUROC (0.91-0.93) for sex-specific tumor-vs-non-tumor panels but small external n and wide CIs support high analysis-domain risk.
appraisal_note: Male-vs-female tumor discrimination panel performed notably worse (AUROC 0.734) than sex-specific tumor-vs-non-tumor panels (AUROC 0.91-0.93); external validation sets are small (n=58/70) with wide bootstrap CIs.

title: Machine learning-based integration of systemic immune-inflammation and nutritional signatures for predicting disease-free survival in upper tract urothelial carcinoma: a multicenter study.
rationale_c1: Four-center retrospective UTUC cohort (n=606) with notable inter-cohort heterogeneity in tumor size, grade and margin status, raising comparability/representativeness concerns.
rationale_c2: Thirteen preoperative hematological indicators were measured via standard clinical laboratory assays.
rationale_c3: Cohort assembly and follow-up (DFS) are clearly reported with complete allocation across training/internal/external sets.
rationale_c4: Multivariate Cox regression identified independent clinical predictors (age, grade, pT stage) for the combined nomogram.
rationale_c5: Preoperative bloodwork and RNU were performed per standard institutional protocol across centers.
criteria_note: MMAT v2018 quantitative non-randomized (4-center retrospective cohort, RSF-based ML score with 2 external validation sets).
probast_rationale: RSF-derived ML Score with SHAP interpretation and data-driven optimal cutoff determined in the training set only (authors flag this as a limitation); C-index 0.71-0.76 across training/validation cohorts with consistent risk stratification.
appraisal_note: Well-conducted multicenter prognostic model (RSF + SHAP + nomogram + DCA) with 2 independent external validation cohorts; authors explicitly discuss the cutoff-derivation limitation.

title: Ribosome biogenesis programs define a three-gene RBscore with prognostic relevance in bladder cancer.
rationale_c1: TCGA-BLCA training (RNA-seq) vs. GSE13507 external validation (microarray) are convenience cross-platform public cohorts; representativeness unclear.
rationale_c2: Differential expression, WGCNA-like candidate gene selection, IHC and RT-qPCR were performed with standard, well-described methods.
rationale_c3: 398/163 cases with complete matched survival data were retained per cohort.
rationale_c4: Multivariable Cox regression retained RBscore and N stage as independent prognostic factors.
rationale_c5: Model selection (95 strategies) and external fixed-model projection followed pre-specified protocol.
criteria_note: MMAT v2018 quantitative non-randomized (TCGA training + GSE13507 external validation, 95-strategy ML model selection, IHC validation n=76).
probast_rationale: StepCox[both]+RSF selected among 95 modeling strategies; training C-index 0.871 attenuated markedly to 0.606 in external validation, and 1/3/5-year AUCs dropped from ~0.92-0.95 (training) to ~0.6-0.7 (external), indicating overfitting/analysis-domain risk.
appraisal_note: Marked attenuation of discrimination from training to external validation (C-index 0.871 to 0.606) is a notable overfitting signal despite otherwise thorough mechanistic/immune/pharmacogenomic characterization and IHC validation.

title: Multidimensional transcriptomic analysis and in vitro experiments dissect the landscape of 2',2',4',4'-Tetrabromodiphenyl ether in bladder cancer progression.
rationale_c1: Combines in vitro cell-line exposure experiments with convenience public cohorts (TCGA-BLCA + 3 GEO datasets); representativeness of a defined patient population is unclear.
rationale_c2: CCK-8, EdU, Transwell, RNA-seq, WGCNA/hdWGCNA and molecular docking are standard, well-described methods.
rationale_c3: 335 TCGA-BLCA cases with survival data plus complete GEO validation datasets were used.
rationale_c4: Nomogram combined the BDERS risk score with age, gender, grade, T and N stage.
rationale_c5: BDE-47 exposure dose (0.1 uM) was justified as physiologically relevant to reported human serum levels.
criteria_note: MMAT v2018 quantitative non-randomized (mechanistic toxicology in vitro study with an embedded 101-combination ML prognostic signature, 3 external validation cohorts).
probast_rationale: BDERS (20-gene risk score) selected via 101 ML-algorithm combinations from a 229-gene BDE-47-interacting candidate pool; C-index only 0.67-0.68 (modest) despite external validation in 3 GEO cohorts, reflecting high analysis-domain risk typical of this corpus.
appraisal_note: Primarily an environmental-toxicant mechanistic study (BDE-47 exposure in vitro); the BDERS prognostic signature is a general TCGA-derived BLCA risk score built from BDE-47-associated genes rather than a model predicting actual patient exposure, so applicability to AI-biomarker/exposure-outcome PICO carries a high-concern exposure-proxy caveat per calibration rule; applies_prediction_appraisal=yes because a formal risk score with C-index/AUC was developed and externally validated.

title: Comprehensive Analysis Based on the Cancer-Immunity Cycle Identifies a Novel Immunosuppressive Subtype of Bladder Cancer.
rationale_c1: Convenience TCGA-BLCA plus GSE166716 cohorts and an own clinical specimen set with sampling method not fully specified; representativeness unclear.
rationale_c2: WGCNA, three ML feature-selection methods (SVM-RFE, RF, plus one more), ssGSEA/CIBERSORT immune profiling and qRT-PCR/Western blot are standard methods.
rationale_c3: Consensus clustering-derived subgroup sample sizes and completeness of survival follow-up for the EIC subtype are not fully detailed in the available text.
rationale_c4: Prognostic network analysis and Cox modeling adjusted for relevant covariates for hub DECICGs.
rationale_c5: Wet-lab knockdown/overexpression assays for BIRC5 were performed per standard protocol.
criteria_note: MMAT v2018 quantitative non-randomized (unsupervised molecular subtyping study with embedded ML hub-gene selection and functional validation).
probast_rationale: Primary output is an unsupervised immunosuppressive molecular subtype (EIC) rather than a single validated risk score; ROC/AUC is reported for hub-gene tumor-vs-normal discrimination and TIDE is used to project ICB response, but no independent survival-validation cohort for the EIC subtype itself is presented.
appraisal_note: Borderline applies_prediction_appraisal call: this is primarily a molecular subtyping/mechanistic paper (EIC immunosuppressive subtype identification via WGCNA+ML+consensus clustering) rather than a conventional single predictive risk score; marked yes per protocol default because hub-gene ROC/AUC and TIDE-based immunotherapy-response prediction are reported, but TRIPOD-AI adherence is weaker than typical prognostic-signature papers in this batch (no dedicated external validation cohort for the subtype/classifier itself).

title: Multi-omics identification of a programmed cell death-related signature and potential target P4HB for bladder cancer based on a 101-combination machine learning and experimental validation.
rationale_c1: Convenience public multi-cohort design (TCGA-BLCA training; GSE13507, GSE37815, GSE166716, GSE154261 validation) across RNA-seq/microarray platforms; representativeness unclear.
rationale_c2: WGCNA, ssGSEA, single-cell RNA-seq, IHC, RT-qPCR, Western blot and functional assays (CCK-8, colony formation, flow cytometry) are standard, well-described methods.
rationale_c3: Training and validation datasets had complete matched survival information as reported.
rationale_c4: Multivariate Cox regression confirmed independent prognostic value of PCDRS alongside age and tumor stage.
rationale_c5: 101-combination ML framework and NRI/IDI benchmarking were applied as pre-specified.
criteria_note: MMAT v2018 quantitative non-randomized (multi-cohort TCGA+GEO training/validation, 101-combination ML signature, single-cell and in vitro P4HB validation).
probast_rationale: 12-gene PCDRS selected from 2126 candidate PCD genes via WGCNA + 101 ML-algorithm combinations; training AUCs strong (0.80-0.84) but external validation more modest (AUC 0.60-0.66, C-index 0.62-0.63), consistent with typical analysis-domain overfitting risk in this corpus.
appraisal_note: Methodologically thorough (WGCNA + 101-combination ML + NRI/IDI benchmarking + single-cell + IHC/functional validation of P4HB), but external AUC/C-index attenuation vs. training indicates moderate overfitting.

title: Identification of a weighted urinary microbial signature for bladder cancer discrimination.
rationale_c1: Small single-center case-control cohort (n=51: 27 BCa, 24 controls), men aged >50 years only, with the BCa group substantially older than controls (73.1 vs 61.6 years), explicitly limiting representativeness and generalizability.
rationale_c2: 16S rRNA sequencing (V3-V6) and Random Forest feature selection are appropriately described and standard.
rationale_c3: Complete taxonomic and outcome (case/control) data were available for all 51 subjects.
rationale_c4: Age was adjusted for via multivariate logistic regression, but other known urobiome confounders (BMI, smoking) were not consistently available, per authors' own limitations statement.
rationale_c5: Urine collection protocol (first-morning, pre-instrumentation) was standardized and applied as intended.
criteria_note: MMAT v2018 quantitative non-randomized (small single-center case-control, no independent validation cohort).
probast_rationale: Feature selection (RF) and WCI weight derivation were performed once on the entire dataset with no independent train/test split or external validation cohort (explicitly stated by authors); only internal 10x5-fold CV and permutation testing mitigate this, so predictor- and analysis-domain risk of bias are high despite strong reported AUCs (90-92%).
appraisal_note: Authors explicitly frame this as a hypothesis-generating biomarker-discovery study lacking an independent validation cohort; feature selection and index weighting were derived on the full dataset with no held-out test set, a substantial methodological limitation for a diagnostic score with AUC ~90%.

title: A machine learning-based epigenetic signature reveals YTHDC1 stabilizes POU5F1 to oppose tumor progression.
rationale_c1: Convenience TCGA-BLCA training cohort with 4 independent public validation cohorts across different platforms (IMvigor210, E-MTAB-4321, GSE31684, GSE48075); representativeness unclear.
rationale_c2: Cox regression on epigenetic-gene expression, single-cell CellChat interaction analysis, RIP-PCR, Western blot and functional knockdown assays are standard, well-described methods.
rationale_c3: Samples lacking primary-tumor status or adequate follow-up were excluded per explicit criteria, with complete data used thereafter.
rationale_c4: Multivariate Cox regression confirmed the signature as independent of sex and age.
rationale_c5: Signature scoring and risk-group assignment were applied identically and as pre-specified across all validation cohorts.
criteria_note: MMAT v2018 quantitative non-randomized (TCGA training with 4 independent external validation cohorts, benchmarked against 101 ML algorithms and 110 published signatures, functional validation of YTHDC1).
probast_rationale: Six-gene signature selected by enumerating combinations of 22 candidate epigenetic genes and choosing the lowest p-value configuration (explicit risk of overfitting/data dredging), though mitigated by validation across 4 independent external cohorts and benchmarking against 101 ML algorithms and 110 published signatures where it consistently outperformed comparators; median risk-score cutoff varied across datasets (authors' acknowledged limitation).
appraisal_note: Among the most extensively benchmarked signatures in this batch (vs. 101 ML algorithms and 110 published signatures across 4 external cohorts); authors explicitly acknowledge cutoff-value instability across platforms as a translational limitation.

title: A systematic characterization of amino acid metabolism-related genes reveals molecular subtypes and a prognostic signature in bladder cancer.
rationale_c1: Combines TCGA/GEO public cohorts with a single-center IHC/clinical cohort (n=41) without explicit stated inclusion/exclusion criteria for representativeness.
rationale_c2: Standard RNA-seq, WGCNA, IHC and functional assay methods with clearly described pipelines.
rationale_c3: Survival/clinical data available and analyzed across three cohorts (TCGA, GSE13507, GSE32894) with consistent follow-up.
rationale_c4: Multivariate Cox regression and nomogram adjust for clinical covariates (age, stage, pT, pN).
rationale_c5: Consistent bioinformatic/experimental pipeline applied uniformly across cohorts and validation experiments.
criteria_note: MMAT v2018 quantitative non-randomized (TCGA+GEO multi-cohort + single-center IHC/functional validation).
probast_rationale: Predictors and outcome well defined; Analysis domain high risk due to massive algorithm search (117 ML combinations via MIME) and median-based risk dichotomization typical of omics signatures.

title: Development and validation of a gemcitabine sensitivity-related long noncoding RNA signature for predicting the prognosis and subtypes of bladder cancer.
rationale_c1: Combines TCGA-BLCA/GEO/IMvigor210 with a prospectively collected single-center tissue cohort (n=163) without explicit eligibility criteria detailed.
rationale_c2: WGCNA, DESeq2, 101 ML algorithm combinations, scRNA-seq and RT-qPCR/functional assays are well described.
rationale_c3: OS/recurrence data available across TCGA training and GSE31684 external validation cohorts.
rationale_c4: Multivariate Cox regression and nomogram incorporate clinical covariates.
rationale_c5: Consistent modeling pipeline applied to training and validation cohorts.
criteria_note: MMAT v2018 quantitative non-randomized (TCGA training + GSE31684 external validation + IMvigor210 + own tissue cohort).
probast_rationale: Analysis domain high risk due to 101-algorithm LOOCV feature/model selection and median-based risk dichotomization typical of this corpus.
appraisal_note: Reports adherence to the TRIPOD reporting checklist explicitly and provides a GitHub code repository (partial transparency) plus a web-based risk calculator.

title: Single-cell transcriptomic analysis and machine learning identify ATAD3A as a key gene that stabilizes mitochondrial-endoplasmic reticulum membranes, promoting bladder cancer progression.
rationale_c1: Uses TCGA/GEO (GSE13507, GSE135337, GSE130001, GSE169455, GSE5287, GSE247185) plus IMvigor210 without explicit eligibility criteria; multi-cohort but retrospective public-database sampling.
rationale_c2: Bulk/single-cell RNA-seq, spatial transcriptomics, IHC (AUC 0.936) and in vitro/in vivo functional assays are well described.
rationale_c3: Survival data available across TCGA-BLCA and GSE13507 with KM/Cox analyses.
rationale_c4: Multivariate Cox regression, nomogram incorporating clinical variables.
rationale_c5: Consistent pipeline applied across bulk, single-cell and validation datasets.
criteria_note: MMAT v2018 quantitative non-randomized (mechanistic single-cell/multi-omics study with embedded LASSO prognostic signature and RF predictive classifier).
probast_rationale: Analysis domain high risk: LASSO 4-gene MAM signature plus separate random forest cisplatin-resistance classifier with SHAP interpretation, selected among candidate genes with limited events-per-variable reporting.
appraisal_note: Primarily a mechanistic single-cell/multi-omics study (MAM/ATAD3A biology) but contains an evaluable predictive component (4-gene MAM prognostic signature with AUC/KM across TCGA, GSE13507, IMvigor210; RF cisplatin-resistance model with external AUC 0.708-0.850 in two validation sets) — applies_prediction_appraisal=yes per calibration default.

title: Transcriptome and single-cell RNA sequencing analysis with 101 machine learning combinations and experimental verification reveals the mechanism of action of mannose metabolism in bladder cancer.
rationale_c1: TCGA-BLCA + GSE13507 + GSE222315 public cohorts without explicit eligibility criteria described.
rationale_c2: DESeq2, SVM/SHAP feature selection, RT-qPCR, WB, IHC and scRNA-seq are clearly described.
rationale_c3: Survival data available in TCGA and GSE13507 with ROC/nomogram analyses.
rationale_c4: Multivariate Cox regression with age, gender, T/N stage; nomogram integrating risk score.
rationale_c5: Consistent SVM/algorithm pipeline applied to training and validation datasets.
criteria_note: MMAT v2018 quantitative non-randomized (TCGA+GEO with 10-algorithm SVM/SHAP feature selection, external validation and functional verification).
probast_rationale: Analysis domain high risk: SVM selected as optimal among 10 algorithms (AUC 0.988 training, near-perfect discrimination suggestive of overfitting) with SHAP-based post-hoc gene selection.
appraisal_note: SVM diagnostic model AUC near-perfect (0.988/0.987) across training and validation datasets — flag as potential overfitting/optimistic performance typical of small feature-selected omics models.

title: Revealing the function and mechanism of piRNA-related genes in bladder cancer through single-cell sequencing and methylation analyses and construction of prognostic features based on consensus clustering.
rationale_c1: TCGA + GSE13507 + GSE135337 public cohorts without explicit eligibility criteria described.
rationale_c2: LASSO/RF/SVM-RFE feature selection, qPCR, methylation-specific PCR and scRNA-seq are well described.
rationale_c3: The LASSO-derived risk-score stratification failed to show a significant survival difference (Fig. 11C), so outcome capture via the intended predictive model is incomplete/ambiguous.
rationale_c4: No adjusted multivariate Cox model is reported for the final risk-score signature; survival significance was only achieved via an unsupervised consensus-clustering post-hoc pivot, not the originally proposed predictive model.
rationale_c5: Consistent experimental/bioinformatic pipeline applied across TCGA, GEO and scRNA-seq datasets.
criteria_note: MMAT v2018 quantitative non-randomized (TCGA+GEO with LASSO/RF/SVM-RFE feature selection; risk-score model underperformed, pivoted to consensus clustering).
probast_rationale: Analysis domain high risk: multi-algorithm feature selection (LASSO/RF/SVM-RFE) from a small candidate gene set; the risk-score prognostic model failed to stratify survival and was superseded post-hoc by unsupervised consensus clustering, indicating unstable/overfit model development.
appraisal_note: Borderline judgment call: the intended risk-score prognostic model (LASSO, 3 piRPGs: MAPK13/INHBA/LAMB2) did not achieve significant survival stratification; authors substituted an unsupervised consensus-clustering grouping that did show significance, which is a weaker/different form of predictive evaluation. Kept applies_prediction_appraisal=yes per corpus calibration default, but PROBAST/TRIPOD-AI judgments reflect this methodological weakness. INHBA also non-significant in external GSE13507 validation for the diagnostic gene panel.

title: A Deep Learning-Generated Mixed Tumor-Stroma Ratio for Prognostic Stratification and Multi-omics Profiling in Bladder Cancer.
rationale_c1: Explicit inclusion/exclusion criteria (Fig. S1) across TCGA (n=379) and 5 multicenter external cohorts (n=1053), with baseline characteristics reported (Table 1).
rationale_c2: CNN tissue classification validated against pathologist ground truth (Cohen's kappa>0.95; ICC=0.90; Bland-Altman); mpMRI radiomics features with reported ICC.
rationale_c3: OS follow-up data available and consistent across TCGA and 5 external cohorts with meta-analysis.
rationale_c4: Multivariate Cox regression and nomogram incorporating N stage; subgroup analyses by NMIBC/MIBC.
rationale_c5: Standardized CNN pipeline (color normalization, patch classification) consistently applied across training/internal/external validation sets.
criteria_note: MMAT v2018 quantitative non-randomized; exceptionally rigorous multicenter deep-learning biomarker study with explicit eligibility criteria and external validation.
probast_rationale: Participants, predictors and outcome domains are low risk given explicit eligibility criteria, blinded pathologist annotation, and standard OS endpoint across a large multicenter cohort. Analysis domain judged unclear (not high) because the core MTSR-OS Cox analysis is robust and externally validated (meta-analysis HR 1.04, 6 cohorts), but the auxiliary mpMRI radiomics classifier for predicting MTSR shows only modest performance (AUC 0.71/0.66) from a small single-center scRNA/radiomics sample, acknowledged as a limitation by the authors.
appraisal_note: Exception to corpus calibration: mmat_overall=high is justified by unusually rigorous design (multicenter, explicit eligibility criteria, pathologist-validated deep-learning ground truth with ICC/kappa, external meta-analysis) rather than a typical convenience-sample omics-mining study. PROBAST_overall_rob kept as unclear (not high) given this rigor, despite the modest-performing ancillary radiomics model.

title: Machine Learning Integration Framework Constructs a Lactylation-Associated Gene Signature to Improve Prognosis in Bladder Cancer.
rationale_c1: TCGA + GSE13507 + GSE32894 public cohorts without explicit eligibility criteria described.
rationale_c2: 101 ML algorithm combinations, RT-qPCR, HPA immunohistochemistry, and functional assays (AHNAK knockdown) are well described.
rationale_c3: Survival data available across TCGA training and two GEO validation cohorts.
rationale_c4: Multivariate Cox regression confirms risk score independence from age and stage.
rationale_c5: Consistent 101-algorithm pipeline applied to training and validation cohorts.
criteria_note: MMAT v2018 quantitative non-randomized (TCGA training + 2 GEO external validation cohorts, 101 ML combinations).
probast_rationale: Analysis domain high risk due to 101-algorithm combination search (CoxBoost+SuperPC selected) and high reported AUCs (0.839-0.880) typical of optimistic in-sample selection in this corpus.

title: Integrated multi-omics analysis identifies DARS2, MRTO4, and MRPL37 as novel biomarkers and potential therapeutic targets for bladder cancer.
rationale_c1: Combines TCGA, GSE13507, GSE135337, IMvigor210, DepMap, FinnGen and eQTLGen without a single unified eligibility framework, though filtering steps are partially described.
rationale_c2: WGCNA, Mfuzz, Mendelian randomization, ROC and scRNA-seq methods are clearly described with parameters.
rationale_c3: Survival data available in TCGA and GSE13507 with consistent follow-up (mean 27.6 and 48.4 months).
rationale_c4: Multivariate/nomogram analysis and MR sensitivity analyses (heterogeneity, pleiotropy) account for confounding.
rationale_c5: Consistent multi-step analytic pipeline (DEGs, WGCNA, Mfuzz, Cox, MR) applied uniformly.
criteria_note: MMAT v2018 quantitative non-randomized (multi-omics integration with Mendelian randomization causal-inference layer).
probast_rationale: Analysis domain high risk: multi-step narrowing from 348 candidate genes (DEGs+WGCNA+Mfuzz+DepMap dependency) to 3 core genes via univariate Cox and MR, a high-dimensionality selection pipeline typical of overfitting risk despite the added MR causal-inference layer.
appraisal_note: Incorporates a Mendelian randomization causal-inference component beyond typical corpus designs; developed an online nomogram tool (partial transparency, no code repository stated).

title: Gene signature for response prediction to immunotherapy and prognostic markers in metastatic urothelial carcinoma.
rationale_c1: Well-defined clinical trial cohorts (IMvigor210, PCD4989g, IMmotion150) with RECIST 1.1-defined response criteria.
rationale_c2: Standardized RNA-seq alignment/quantification (kallisto, DESeq2) and rigorous feature-selection/classifier-training methodology.
rationale_c3: Some samples excluded due to missing PD-L1 IHC or missing HLA-E data, slightly reducing completeness for comparator signatures.
rationale_c4: Extensive comparison against six established signatures, TMB, and ablation studies control for confounding/benchmarking bias.
rationale_c5: Consistent training/testing pipeline (5-fold CV, domain adaptation) applied uniformly across cohorts.
criteria_note: MMAT v2018 quantitative non-randomized (retrospective transcriptomic reanalysis of prospective immunotherapy clinical trial cohorts).
probast_rationale: Participants/predictors/outcome low risk given clear RECIST-defined trial cohorts and standardized RNA-seq; Analysis domain high risk due to reduction of ~17,000 genes to 49 via multi-step feature selection (BW-ratio + unsupervised domain adaptation) relative to a modest sample size (n=298 train), a classic high-dimensional overfitting scenario despite external validation.
appraisal_note: Strongest TRIPOD-AI reporting in this batch: independent external clinical-trial test set (PCD4989g, AUC 0.75) plus additional unseen GEO datasets and an ablation study isolating the contribution of domain adaptation. Data access restricted via EGA (partial transparency).

title: Bladder cancer diagnostic and prognostic models from DNA methylation by multi algorithm machine learning.
rationale_c1: Integrates TCGA tissue (n=416/21), a very small urine cohort (GSE120288, n=12), a blood cohort from a prior study, and validation sets (GSE111933, GSE13507) without unified eligibility criteria.
rationale_c2: ChAMP-based differential methylation analysis, six ML algorithms, Lasso/logistic and Cox-Lasso modeling, plus Co-IP/ChIP-seq mechanistic validation are clearly described.
rationale_c3: Diagnostic and prognostic outcome data available with reasonable completeness across TCGA and validation cohorts.
rationale_c4: Cox-Lasso and logistic regression models adjust for relevant covariates; NMIBC/MIBC subgroup analyses performed.
rationale_c5: Consistent multi-sample (tissue/blood/urine) methylation pipeline applied across all cohorts.
criteria_note: MMAT v2018 quantitative non-randomized (multi-sample-type DNA methylation diagnostic/prognostic ML models with mechanistic TET2/C1QTNF6 validation).
probast_rationale: Participants domain high risk: the urine-based diagnostic validation cohort is extremely small (n=12, GSE120288), substantially undermining representativeness/generalizability of a key diagnostic component. Analysis domain high risk given a multi-step 173-gene to 11-gene to final-model narrowing across three sample types using six ML algorithms.
appraisal_note: Preprint-style 'Article in Press' formatting noted in extracted text (unedited manuscript, may contain errors per publisher disclaimer). Urine validation cohort extremely small (n=12) despite otherwise strong tissue-based diagnostic performance (AUC 0.957); flagged as elevated PROBAST Participants risk.

title: Integrative pan-cancer analysis of intratumoral microbial communities for biomarker discovery and diagnostic modeling.
rationale_c1: Multi-study inclusion and QC pipeline for 2839 samples described.
rationale_c2: 16S QIIME2/DADA2 and ML classification methods fit diagnostic aim.
rationale_c3: Merged public cohorts; batch/source effects acknowledged.
rationale_c4: PERMANOVA stratified by source; sensitivity analysis but residual batch risk.
rationale_c5: Stratified 5-fold CV plus independent CAMS validation cohort (541).
probast_rationale: Pan-cancer pooled data; batch heterogeneity limits bias/applicability judgment.
appraisal_note: Pan-cancer diagnostic model; bladder is one of nine types (not GU-focused).

title: Construction and mechanistic exploration of a ferroptosis related gene based prognostic model for cisplatin resistance in bladder cancer.
rationale_c1: Only 44 TCGA cisplatin-treated cases define chemoresponse; eligibility for that subset is unclear.

rationale_c3: Training on GSE32894 and tiny chemoresponse subset limits representativeness.
rationale_c4: Multiple ML filters and nomogram tuning on same training data; weak external AUC (~0.68-0.71).
rationale_c5: OS and time-dependent ROC in GSE32894 and GSE13507 are reported.
criteria_note: MMAT v2018 quantitative non-randomized (retrospective transcriptomic cohorts).
probast_rationale: Small retrospective chemoresponse series; tri-algorithm feature mining on training cohort; extreme HR in KM raises overfitting concern.

title: Constructing a bladder cancer prognostic model related to exosome using machine learning and identifying THBS1 as a potential target.
rationale_c1: TCGA + GSE13507 public cohorts without explicit eligibility criteria described.
rationale_c2: 101 ML algorithm combinations, molecular docking, qRT-PCR, WB and in vivo lung metastasis assays are well described.
rationale_c3: Survival data available across TCGA training and GSE13507 external validation.
rationale_c4: Multivariate Cox regression confirms risk score independence; nomogram integrates clinical variables.
rationale_c5: Consistent 101-algorithm pipeline applied to training and validation cohorts.
criteria_note: MMAT v2018 quantitative non-randomized (TCGA training + GSE13507 external validation, 101 ML combinations).
probast_rationale: Analysis domain high risk: 15 genes selected from 132 DEGs via univariate Cox (p<0.05) then 101 ML combinations; model discrimination is modest (average C-index 0.614), and authors themselves note predictive performance was surpassed by age alone, indicating limited added prognostic value.
appraisal_note: Model discrimination modest (C-index 0.614; 1/3/5-year AUC 0.648-0.724); authors explicitly acknowledge the model's predictive accuracy is surpassed by age alone among clinical variables — weaker predictive performance than most of this batch.

title: Imidacloprid contributes to bladder cancer progression: preliminary evidence based on network toxicology, machine learning and molecular docking.
rationale_c1: TCGA (random 3:1 train/test split) plus GSE13507/GSE31684 external cohorts, without explicit patient eligibility criteria stated.
rationale_c2: DESeq2 differential expression, 10 ML algorithms with Brier-score calibration, molecular docking (CB-DOCK2), and in vitro exposure assays (colony formation, wound healing, transwell) are well described.

rationale_c4: Multivariate Cox regression, nomogram, and subgroup analyses by stage/sex/age control for confounding.
rationale_c5: Consistent IMI exposure concentration (10 ng/mL, based on occupational biomonitoring data) applied uniformly in vitro.
criteria_note: MMAT v2018 quantitative non-randomized (network toxicology + ML prognostic model + in vitro exposure experiments).
probast_rationale: Analysis domain high risk: 531 CTD-derived imidacloprid-related genes narrowed to 138 DEIRGs then to a 5-gene model via 10 ML algorithms and multivariate Cox with a modest test-cohort size (n=96). Applicability flagged high concern because the study's primary framing is an environmental exposure/toxicology mechanism (pesticide-gene interaction) rather than a direct clinical biomarker-discovery design matching AIBIO_GU's PCC.
appraisal_note: Primary framing is environmental toxicology (imidacloprid/pesticide exposure mechanism via network toxicology and molecular docking) with an embedded DEIRG-based prognostic ML model (average C-index 0.766; time-dependent AUC 0.60-0.72) evaluated across TCGA/GSE13507/GSE31684. applies_prediction_appraisal=yes per the prognostic component and calibration default, but probast_overall_applicability flagged as high concern (exposure-proxy design) per the codebook's applicability rule; this does not change screening/eligibility per protocol.

appraisal_note: One of the most extensively validated signatures in the batch (11 independent cohorts, benchmarked vs 58 published models); still high analysis ROB per calibration default for massive ML search.
