rationale_c1: Discovery (9 IUP, 12 PUC, 10 NU) and IHC cohort (25 IUP, 16 PUC) match diagnostic aim.
rationale_c2: LC-MS/MS proteomics and IHC validation are fit-for-purpose for biomarker discovery.
rationale_c3: Rare entities, single-center archival series; small discovery groups limit representativeness.
rationale_c4: SVM feature selection on discovery set then IHC test; cutoff transfer not fully independent.
rationale_c5: Authors report small validation n and plan multi-institution confirmation.
criteria_note: MMAT v2018 quantitative descriptive (proteomic case series with comparative groups).
probast_rationale: Small single-center FFPE series; ML on discovery proteome with same-institution IHC validation and H-score cutoff optimization.
appraisal_note: Borderline: TCGA survival mentions for risk subgroups; primary appraisal targets diagnostic PYGB IHC model (AUROC 0.923).

title: A nomogram combined with radiomics features, albuminuria, and metabolic syndrome to predict the risk of myometrial invasion of bladder cancer.
rationale_c1: Single-center retrospective cohort n=100, convenience sample.
rationale_c2: Multi-parameter CT radiomics + albuminuria/metabolic syndrome clinical factors appropriately assessed.
rationale_c3: Complete data for included patients (train 70/validation 30).
rationale_c4: Albuminuria and metabolic syndrome identified as independent factors via multivariable analysis, partially addressing confounding, but extent of adjustment unclear from abstract.
rationale_c5: Radiomics+SVM+nomogram pipeline applied per stated TRIPOD-informed protocol.
criteria_note: MMAT non-randomized (Hong 2018); explicitly followed TRIPOD reporting checklist.
probast_rationale: 1223 texture features from n=100 single-center cohort with small validation set (n=30); TRIPOD checklist followed is a reporting strength.
appraisal_note: Explicit TRIPOD checklist adherence noted in Methods, a positive reporting signal; still single-center small-sample study.

title: A Novel CpG Methylation Risk Indicator for Predicting Prognosis in Bladder Cancer.
rationale_c1: TCGA cohort (n=357) randomly split into training/internal validation; convenience public cohort, no external dataset.
rationale_c2: CpG methylation and clinical stage/sex/age appropriately assessed.
rationale_c3: Missing-data handling for methylation array data not detailed.
rationale_c4: No formal confounder adjustment beyond nomogram covariates.
rationale_c5: LASSO + SVM-RFE overlap pipeline applied as described.
probast_rationale: Internal-only validation (no independent external cohort); 8-CpG methylation signature.
appraisal_note: Only internal (TCGA-split) validation; no independent external cohort reported.

title: Identification of CNGB1 as a Predictor of Response to Neoadjuvant Chemotherapy in Muscle-Invasive Bladder Cancer.
rationale_c1: Discovery cohort of only 30 MIBC cases explicitly and deliberately selected for extreme response phenotypes (exquisitely strong responders vs marked resistance), a highly non-representative extreme-groups design.
rationale_c2: Gene expression profiling and IHC appropriately assessed.
rationale_c3: Small sample sizes across discovery (n=30) and validation cohorts (n=26, n=99) limit completeness assessment.
rationale_c4: No adjustment for confounders in this extreme-phenotype discovery design.
rationale_c5: RGIFE ML feature elimination applied as described.
criteria_note: MMAT non-randomized (Hong 2018); extreme-phenotype discovery design is a notable limitation.
probast_rationale: Extreme-phenotype 'exquisitely selected' discovery cohort (n=30) reporting 100% predictive accuracy is a classic overfitting red flag; two independent validation cohorts partially mitigate.
appraisal_note: Discovery cohort selection is deliberately non-representative (extreme responders/non-responders) inflating apparent predictive accuracy (100% reported); flagged as high risk of optimistic bias despite validation cohorts.

title: Radiomic assessment as a method for predicting tumor mutation burden (TMB) of bladder cancer patients: a feasibility study.
rationale_c1: TCIA/TCGA-BLCA cohort n=75, convenience public sample, explicitly termed a 'feasibility study'.
rationale_c2: Radiomic features and TMB status appropriately assessed.
rationale_c3: Complete data for the 75 included patients.
rationale_c4: No adjustment for confounders; small single-dataset analysis.
rationale_c5: Unsupervised clustering + LASSO/backward stepwise regression applied as described.
probast_rationale: Small n=75 feasibility study without independent external validation; authors explicitly call for future larger studies.
appraisal_note: Explicitly self-described 'feasibility study' with no external validation cohort; conclusions should be considered preliminary.

title: A Novel Nomogram Based on Machine Learning-Pathomics Signature and Neutrophil to Lymphocyte Ratio for Survival Prediction of Bladder Cancer Patients.
rationale_c1: TCGA (n=406) + Shanghai General Hospital (n=508 WSIs total) cross-validated cohorts; convenience sample.
rationale_c2: WSI pathomics features and NLR appropriately assessed.
rationale_c3: Complete data for included patients across both cohorts.
rationale_c4: No formal confounder adjustment beyond univariate/multivariate Cox.
rationale_c5: Pathomics feature selection + nomogram pipeline applied as described.
probast_rationale: Cross-validated across TCGA and an independent institutional cohort, a relative strength.
appraisal_note: External institutional validation (General cohort) is a strength; still single external site plus TCGA.

title: Combining Multiparametric MRI Radiomics Signature With the Vesical Imaging-Reporting and Data System (VI-RADS) Score to Preoperatively Differentiate Muscle Invasion of Bladder Cancer.
rationale_c1: Single-center retrospective cohort n=185, convenience sample.
rationale_c2: mpMRI radiomics + VI-RADS score appropriately assessed.
rationale_c3: Complete data for included patients (train 129/validation 56).
rationale_c4: No broader confounder adjustment beyond logistic regression; single institution.
rationale_c5: mRMR feature selection + LASSO/SVM/RF classifiers applied as described.
probast_rationale: Single-center cohort with internal train/validation split only; three classifiers compared.
appraisal_note: Muscle-invasion differentiation nomogram; internal validation only.

title: Clinical use of machine learning-based pathomics signature for diagnosis and survival prediction of bladder cancer.
rationale_c1: Shanghai General Hospital + TCGA cohorts (643 images total), convenience sample.
rationale_c2: H&E pathomics features and clinical risk stratification appropriately assessed.
rationale_c3: Complete data for included patients across cohorts.
rationale_c4: No formal confounder adjustment beyond nomogram covariates.
rationale_c5: Cross-verified ML pathomics diagnosis/prognosis pipeline applied as described.
probast_rationale: External validation cohort included (General cohort separate from TCGA), a relative strength.
appraisal_note: External institutional validation cohort present.

title: Identification of a ten-long noncoding RNA signature for predicting the survival and immune status of patients with bladder urothelial carcinoma based on the GEO database: a superior machine learning model.
rationale_c1: GEO-based cohorts (BRB-ArrayTools discovery + 3 validation datasets); convenience public cohorts.
rationale_c2: lncRNA expression and immune-infiltration measures appropriately assessed.
rationale_c3: Missing-data handling across multiple GEO datasets not detailed.
rationale_c4: No formal confounder adjustment beyond Cox regression.
rationale_c5: Random survival forest-variable hunting (RSF-VH) pipeline applied as described.
probast_rationale: 10-lncRNA signature validated across 3 GEO datasets, a relative strength despite typical high analysis ROB.
appraisal_note: Multiple validation datasets is a relative strength for this signature.

title: Biomarkers of the Response to Immune Checkpoint Inhibitors in Metastatic Urothelial Carcinoma.
rationale_c1: Retrospective mUC cohort (source/sample size not fully detailed at abstract level, likely public ICI-treated dataset); convenience sample.
rationale_c2: DEGs between ICI responders/non-responders and OS appropriately assessed.
rationale_c3: Missing-data handling not detailed.
rationale_c4: No formal confounder adjustment beyond LASSO-selected genes.
rationale_c5: LASSO on top up/down-regulated DEGs (pre-filtered) applied as described.
probast_rationale: Feature pre-filtering (top 20 up/down DEGs) before LASSO risks optimistic performance; training/testing/combined cohort structure partially mitigates.
appraisal_note: Two-stage feature selection (DEG pre-filter then LASSO) increases risk of overoptimistic model performance.

title: Development of a noninvasive tool to preoperatively evaluate the muscular invasiveness of bladder cancer using a radiomics approach.
rationale_c1: Single-center retrospective cohort n=199, convenience sample.
rationale_c2: MRI radiomics (whole lesion + basal part) appropriately assessed.
rationale_c3: Complete data for included patients (train 130/validation 69).
rationale_c4: Clinical predictor (tumor size) added via multivariable logistic regression but broader confounder control unclear.
rationale_c5: LASSO radiomics signature + nomogram pipeline applied as described.
probast_rationale: Single-center cohort with internal split only (no independent external validation).
appraisal_note: Muscular invasiveness nomogram; internal validation only, single-center.

title: A predictive nomogram for individualized recurrence stratification of bladder cancer using multiparametric MRI and clinical risk factors.
rationale_c1: Single-center cohort n=71, small convenience sample.
rationale_c2: mpMRI radiomics + clinical risk factors appropriately assessed.
rationale_c3: Complete data for included patients (train 50/validation 21).
rationale_c4: Clinical factors (MIS, age, grade, etc.) included but formal confounder adjustment beyond SVM-RFE/LR unclear.
rationale_c5: SVM-RFE + logistic regression pipeline applied as described.
probast_rationale: Very small cohort (n=71) with tiny validation set (n=21); 1872 candidate features.
appraisal_note: Small sample recurrence-prediction nomogram; internal validation only.

title: Development and Validation of an MRI-Based Radiomics Signature for the Preoperative Prediction of Lymph Node Metastasis in Bladder Cancer.
rationale_c1: Single-center cohort n=103, convenience sample.
rationale_c2: MRI radiomics features for LN metastasis appropriately assessed.
rationale_c3: Complete data for included patients (train 69/validation 34).
rationale_c4: MRI-reported LN status included as covariate but broader confounder control unclear.
rationale_c5: LASSO radiomics signature + nomogram pipeline applied as described.
probast_rationale: Small single-center cohort (n=103) with small validation set (n=34); authors explicitly note external validation still required.
appraisal_note: Authors explicitly state external validation is further required prior to clinical implementation.

title: The application of artificial intelligence to microarray data: identification of a novel gene signature to identify bladder cancer progression.
rationale_c1: Discovery microarray cohort n=66 tumors, small convenience sample; validation IHC cohort n=262 larger.
rationale_c2: Gene expression (microarray) and IHC protein expression appropriately assessed.
rationale_c3: Missing-data handling not detailed for older (2009-era) dataset.
rationale_c4: No formal confounder adjustment; comparison of AI vs statistical gene selection methods only.
rationale_c5: NeuroFuzzy Modeling + ANN pipeline applied as described.
probast_rationale: 200 genes pre-selected by statistical correlation before AI analysis (double-dipping risk); small discovery cohort (n=66) though validation cohort reasonably sized (n=262).
appraisal_note: Older (2009) study; AI-gene-selection pipeline followed by IHC validation in a larger independent cohort (n=262) is a relative strength, but feature pre-selection via statistical correlation before AI analysis is a methodological limitation.

title: Dietary Polyphenol Acteoside-Related Molecular Signatures in Clear Cell Renal Cell Carcinoma: Multi-Omics Profiling and Functional Validation of IMPDH1.
rationale_c1: Multi-omics (bulk/single-cell/spatial) public ccRCC cohorts; convenience samples.
rationale_c2: Acteoside-target-derived signatures and clinical outcomes appropriately assessed.
rationale_c3: Missing-data handling for merged multi-omics datasets not detailed.
rationale_c4: No formal confounder adjustment beyond cross-cohort benchmarking.
rationale_c5: Multiple ML strategies benchmarked; 10-gene prognostic model with cross-cohort validation, IMPDH1 functionally validated in vitro.
probast_rationale: 10-gene model retained predictive performance across independent cohorts; functional validation of IMPDH1 supports biological plausibility despite typical high analysis ROB.
appraisal_note: Functional in-vitro validation of IMPDH1 (knockdown/overexpression) strengthens biological plausibility beyond typical bioinformatics-only signatures.

title: Integrative multi-omics identifies PANX2 as a ferroptosis suppressor and potential therapeutic target in clear cell renal cell carcinoma.
rationale_c1: scRNA-seq + bulk + spatial transcriptomic public ccRCC cohorts; convenience samples.
rationale_c2: Ferroptosis-related gene features and survival outcomes appropriately assessed.
rationale_c3: Missing-data handling for multi-omics integration not detailed.
rationale_c4: No formal confounder adjustment beyond independent-cohort model evaluation.
rationale_c5: ML-based feature selection producing 4-gene risk model + nomogram, PANX2 extensively functionally validated (knockdown, xenografts, murine model).
probast_rationale: Consistent predictive performance in training and external validation cohorts; extensive functional/mechanistic validation of PANX2 is a notable strength.
appraisal_note: Extensive in vivo/in vitro mechanistic validation (xenografts, immunocompetent murine model) beyond typical corpus signature papers.

title: NECSO-based classification predicts immunotherapy efficacy and identifies FLAD1 as therapeutic target in kidney renal clear cell carcinoma.
rationale_c1: TCGA discovery + multiple independent ICI-treated/pan-cancer/single-cell validation cohorts; convenience samples.
rationale_c2: NECSO-related gene features, immune microenvironment and ICI response appropriately assessed.
rationale_c3: Missing-data handling across multiple validation datasets not detailed.
rationale_c4: No formal confounder adjustment beyond multi-cohort benchmarking.
rationale_c5: NMF clustering + ML-derived NECSOS score pipeline applied and validated in several independent ICI cohorts, FLAD1 extensively functionally validated.
probast_rationale: Validated in diverse pan-cancer ICI cohorts and single-cell datasets; extensive FLAD1 functional characterization is a notable strength.
appraisal_note: Broad external validation across multiple ICI-treated cohorts (pan-cancer) and functional validation of FLAD1.

title: Development and validation of an integrated machine learning model for recurrence-free survival prediction in clear cell renal cell carcinoma.
rationale_c1: 4-center retrospective cohort n=1284 (train 738/internal validation 317/external test 229); larger and more diverse than most corpus studies but still retrospective convenience sampling.
rationale_c2: Clinical, radiomics (CT) and deep-learning (3D-ViT) descriptors appropriately assessed.
rationale_c3: Complete data reported across training/internal validation/external test splits.
rationale_c4: Cox regression used for clinical feature selection but no broader formal confounder adjustment across the integrated pipeline.
rationale_c5: Radiomics + DL (3D-ViT) + clinical nomogram selected from 8 ML algorithms via 5-fold cross-validation, with a genuinely independent external test cohort.
probast_rationale: Notably robust design: 4-center cohort with a true independent external test cohort (n=229) and consistent AUC 0.85-0.94 across splits; still uses 8-algorithm model selection which carries some analysis risk though mitigated by external testing.
appraisal_note: Among the most methodologically rigorous studies in this batch: multicenter design with genuine external test cohort; deviates from the typical high-PROBAST-ROB default given this external validation rigor (flagged explicitly).

title: Integrative Multi-Transcriptomic Uncovers Actionable Signatures and Drug Repurposing Candidates for ccRCC-Hypertension Comorbidity.
rationale_c1: TCGA-KIRC transcriptomic cohort integrated with GeneCards hypertension gene list; convenience public cohort.
rationale_c2: DEHRGs, WGCNA modules and diagnostic/survival outcomes appropriately assessed.
rationale_c3: Missing-data handling for TCGA/GeneCards integration not detailed.
rationale_c4: Comorbidity (hypertension) is the analytic focus itself rather than a controlled confounder, raising an applicability rather than an internal-validity concern.
rationale_c5: WGCNA + ML + Mendelian randomization pipeline applied as described; in vitro drug validation performed.
probast_rationale: Diagnostic model (tumor vs normal) based on 4 hub genes; Mendelian randomization used to strengthen causal inference is a methodological positive.
appraisal_note: Comorbidity-focused design (ccRCC-hypertension) per calibration rule 5: applicability concern flagged rather than reclassifying eligibility; MR analysis is a methodological strength.

title: Single-Cell and Machine Learning Analyses Identify MYDGF as an Immune-Related Biomarker Associated With the Tumor Microenvironment in Clear Cell Renal Cell Carcinoma.
rationale_c1: scRNA-seq (GSE156632, n=12 samples) + TCGA-KIRC bulk cohort; convenience public samples.
rationale_c2: MYDGF expression, immune-checkpoint and pathway activity appropriately assessed.
rationale_c3: Missing-data handling for merged scRNA/bulk datasets not detailed.
rationale_c4: No formal confounder adjustment; single-gene mechanistic focus with an exploratory gene set.
rationale_c5: LASSO Cox pipeline used to derive a preliminary 19-gene MYDGF-related prognostic set, explicitly described by the authors as requiring further validation.
probast_rationale: Authors explicitly characterize the 19-gene prognostic set as preliminary and requiring further validation; primary contribution is mechanistic (MYDGF single biomarker) rather than a finished prediction model.
appraisal_note: Prognostic gene set explicitly flagged by the authors themselves as preliminary/unvalidated; applies_prediction_appraisal marked yes per the corpus 'when in doubt, appraise' rule but treat PROBAST/TRIPOD judgments as provisional given this is a secondary/exploratory model in a primarily mechanistic biomarker paper.

title: Integrated multi-omics analysis reveals folate metabolism-related genes as prognostic markers and therapeutic targets in clear cell renal cell carcinoma.
rationale_c1: TCGA-KIRC + public multi-omics integration; convenience public cohort.
rationale_c2: Folate-metabolism gene expression and immune-phenotype features appropriately assessed.
rationale_c3: Missing-data handling for multi-omics integration not detailed.
rationale_c4: No formal confounder adjustment beyond cross-cohort scoring system evaluation.
rationale_c5: Multi-omics ML-derived FMRG scoring system applied and validated as described.
probast_rationale: FMRG score construction with functional exploration of key genes; typical high analysis ROB from feature-heavy multi-omics pipeline.
appraisal_note: Standard multi-omics prognostic signature paper for this corpus.

title: Radiomics analysis of CT imaging for predicting MIT family translocation renal cell carcinoma: a multicenter retrospective clinical study.
rationale_c1: Multicenter retrospective cohort n=746 (2 training centers n=539/3 validation centers n=207); rare-subtype (MIT-RCC, n=77) vs other RCC (n=669) yields marked class imbalance.
rationale_c2: CT radiomics features (tumor + renal parenchyma ROIs) appropriately assessed.
rationale_c3: Complete data reported for training/validation cohorts.
rationale_c4: Age and clinical stage incorporated but class imbalance (77 vs 669) not explicitly addressed via resampling or weighting in the abstract-level description.
rationale_c5: LASSO feature selection + logistic regression nomogram applied and externally validated across 3 additional centers.
probast_rationale: Genuine external multicenter validation (3 separate centers) is a strength; marked class imbalance for the rare MIT-RCC subtype raises analysis-domain concern.
appraisal_note: Multicenter external validation across 3 additional centers; class imbalance for rare MIT-RCC subtype (77/746) is a notable analysis-domain concern.

title: Integrative bulk and single-cell transcriptome analyses reveals manganese metabolism-related prognostic genes in clear cell renal cell carcinoma with experimental validation.
rationale_c1: Public bulk + single-cell ccRCC transcriptomic datasets; convenience cohorts.
rationale_c2: Manganese-metabolism gene features and immune infiltration appropriately assessed.
rationale_c3: Missing-data handling for merged public datasets not detailed.
rationale_c4: No formal confounder adjustment beyond nomogram covariates.
rationale_c5: Univariate Cox + ML feature selection pipeline applied as described; RT-qPCR functional validation performed.
probast_rationale: 2-gene (MPPED2/PLAU) risk model with nomogram; RT-qPCR validation supports biological plausibility.
appraisal_note: RT-qPCR expression validation is a relative strength typical of this corpus.

title: Integrated bulk and single-cell transcriptomics reveals TREH as a novel protective biomarker and prognostic predictor in clear cell renal cell carcinoma.
rationale_c1: TCGA-KIRC cohort with 70/30 internal train/test split; convenience public cohort, no independent external cohort.
rationale_c2: TREH expression and clinical/pathological features appropriately assessed.
rationale_c3: Complete data for the 70/30 internal split.
rationale_c4: No formal confounder adjustment beyond nomogram covariates.
rationale_c5: WGCNA + LASSO + GBM pipeline applied as described; extensive in vitro/in vivo functional validation of TREH.
probast_rationale: Extensive functional validation (in vitro/in vivo) of TREH is a strength; only internal TCGA train/test split used, no independent external cohort.
appraisal_note: No independent external validation cohort reported (only internal TCGA 70/30 split); functional validation is otherwise strong.

title: Decoding the Sphingolipid Landscape of Clear Cell Renal Cell Carcinoma: A Single-Cell-Guided Prognostic Model Built With 101 Machine Learning.
rationale_c1: Multiple public cohorts (GEO single-cell + Xena/ArrayExpress/ICGC bulk); convenience samples.
rationale_c2: Sphingolipid-metabolism-related characteristic genes appropriately assessed via NMF and bulk transcriptomics.
rationale_c3: Missing-data handling across the many merged public datasets not detailed.
rationale_c4: No formal confounder adjustment beyond independent-cohort comparison.
rationale_c5: 101 machine-learning combinations benchmarked; final Lasso+SuperPC 12-gene signature validated across independent cohorts.
probast_rationale: 101-combination ML benchmarking is a hallmark of expected high analysis ROB per calibration rule 3, despite multi-cohort validation.
appraisal_note: Very large model-search space (101 ML combinations); typical high analysis ROB per frozen calibration rule 3.

title: Integrated bioinformatics and experimental validation identify aging-related prognostic genes in clear cell renal cell carcinoma.
rationale_c1: TCGA-ccRCC cohort; convenience public cohort, no independent external validation cohort.
rationale_c2: Aging-related DEGs and clinical outcomes appropriately assessed.
rationale_c3: Missing-data handling not detailed.
rationale_c4: No formal confounder adjustment beyond risk-model covariates.
rationale_c5: ML-based screening of 7 ARGs applied as described; RT-qPCR validation performed with noted discrepancies for FOXM1 and CDKN2A.
probast_rationale: RT-qPCR validation partially contradicted bioinformatic predictions for 2 of 5 tested genes (FOXM1, CDKN2A), a notable data-quality caveat.
appraisal_note: RT-qPCR discordance for FOXM1 and CDKN2A vs bioinformatic prediction should be flagged as a validation weakness; no independent external validation cohort.

title: Integrating Bulk and Single-Cell RNA-Seq Reveals Glycolysis-Associated Macrophages and Its Related Tumor Subgroup Signatures to Predict Prognosis and Therapy in Clear Cell Renal Cell Carcinoma.
rationale_c1: Public GEO single-cell (GSE178481) + TCGA-KIRC bulk cohort; convenience samples.
rationale_c2: Glycolysis-macrophage subpopulation features and gene signature appropriately assessed.
rationale_c3: Missing-data handling for merged single-cell/bulk datasets not detailed.
rationale_c4: No formal confounder adjustment beyond risk-group stratification.
rationale_c5: hdWGCNA + 101 ML methods pipeline applied to derive 6-gene signature as described.
probast_rationale: 101-method ML benchmarking (as in similar papers in this batch) is a hallmark of expected high analysis ROB per calibration rule 3.
appraisal_note: Very large model-search space (101 ML combinations); typical high analysis ROB per frozen calibration rule 3.

title: Identification of a prognostic signature based on ammonia metabolism-related genes in clear cell renal cell carcinoma: an integrated analysis of bulk and single-cell transcriptomics.
rationale_c1: Public bulk + single-cell ccRCC transcriptomic datasets; convenience cohorts.
rationale_c2: Ammonia-death-related gene features and immune infiltration appropriately assessed.
rationale_c3: Missing-data handling for merged datasets not detailed.
rationale_c4: No formal confounder adjustment beyond risk-group covariates.
rationale_c5: ML-based screening pipeline applied to derive 6-gene signature; RT-qPCR validation performed.
probast_rationale: 6-gene ammonia-metabolism signature with RT-qPCR confirmation of upregulation; typical high analysis ROB from feature-heavy pipeline.
appraisal_note: Standard ammonia-metabolism prognostic signature paper for this corpus.

title: Integrating single-cell multi-omics and machine learning to reveal triaptosis heterogeneity in clear cell renal cell carcinoma.
rationale_c1: Public single-cell + bulk ccRCC transcriptomic/spatial datasets; convenience cohorts.
rationale_c2: Triaptosis-activity features across cell populations appropriately assessed via scRNA-seq/spatial transcriptomics.
rationale_c3: Missing-data handling for merged multi-omics datasets not detailed.
rationale_c4: No formal confounder adjustment beyond independent-cohort model evaluation.
rationale_c5: 10 ML algorithms benchmarked to derive a 4-gene prognostic signature, validated for prognosis, immunotherapy guidance and chemotherapy response.
probast_rationale: 10-algorithm ML benchmarking to derive a compact 4-gene signature; validated across multiple clinical-utility axes (prognosis, immunotherapy, chemo response).
appraisal_note: Novel triaptosis cell-death concept (2024 discovery) applied to ccRCC; signature validated across prognosis, immunotherapy and chemosensitivity endpoints.

title: Integrated multi-omics analysis of neutrophil extracellular trap-related genes in renal cell carcinoma using bioinformatics and machine learning.
rationale_c1: 5 pooled GEO RCC datasets; convenience cohorts spanning multiple RCC histological subtypes (not exclusively ccRCC).
rationale_c2: NET-related gene expression, immune infiltration and molecular subtypes appropriately assessed.
rationale_c3: Missing-data handling for merged multi-dataset integration not detailed.
rationale_c4: No formal confounder adjustment beyond WGCNA/ML module cross-referencing.
rationale_c5: LASSO/SVM-RFE/RF triple-algorithm overlap pipeline applied to derive an 8-gene NET signature, validated in independent TCGA-KIRC cohort.
probast_rationale: Very high reported diagnostic AUCs (0.987-0.989) for the 8-gene signature raise some concern for overoptimism typical of small-panel diagnostic classifiers; independent TCGA-KIRC validation partially mitigates.
appraisal_note: Cohort spans multiple RCC histological subtypes (not ccRCC-exclusive per abstract), broadening applicability but reducing histologic specificity; very high reported AUCs (~0.99) warrant cautious interpretation.

title: An interpretable machine learning model based on habitat radiomics combined with deep learning for predicting the WHO/ISUP grade of patients with clear cell renal cell carcinoma.
rationale_c1: Retrospective 2-institution cohort n=646, convenience sample.
rationale_c2: Enhanced CT habitat radiomics, deep-learning and clinical features appropriately assessed.
rationale_c3: Complete data reported for training/validation/test splits.
rationale_c4: Age, tumor size, and necrosis identified as independent predictors but broader confounder adjustment beyond multivariate regression unclear.
rationale_c5: K-means habitat clustering + 2D/2.5D DL + LR fusion model applied as described, with SHAP interpretability analysis.
probast_rationale: Complex multi-component pipeline (habitat radiomics + DL fusion) increases analysis-domain risk despite SHAP interpretability efforts and held-out test set.
appraisal_note: SHAP interpretability analysis is a positive transparency/reporting feature not seen in most other papers in this batch.

title: A lactylation-related gene signature predicts prognosis and immunotherapy response in clear cell renal cell carcinoma based on machine learning and multi-omics analysis.
rationale_c1: Convenience public cohorts (TCGA-KIRC + E-MTAB-1980); representativeness of ccRCC/RCC population unclear.
rationale_c2: Transcriptomic/clinical measurements and survival endpoints are standard and fit-for-purpose.
rationale_c3: Public cohorts report survival status and follow-up adequately for included cases.
rationale_c4: Heavy ML algorithm screening/median-split risk stratification with limited independent confounder adjustment.
rationale_c5: Bioinformatic pipeline and (where applicable) in vitro/experimental validation applied as described.
probast_rationale: Convenience TCGA/GEO cohorts, median-split risk score, and extensive ML algorithm competition risk overfitting; predictors/outcome well defined.

title: Multiphase CT-based deep learning radiomics nomogram models for preoperative WHO/ISUP grading of clear cell renal cell carcinoma: a two-center validation study.
rationale_c1: Retrospective single/multi-center recruitment (two-center, n=1499); selection bias plausible.
rationale_c2: Radiomics extraction (IBSI-standard) and clinicopathologic/reference-standard outcome measures are appropriate.
rationale_c3: Pathologic/follow-up outcome data reported for included cases.
rationale_c4: Multivariable clinical+radiomics model partially addresses confounding, though feature selection is data-driven.
rationale_c5: Imaging acquisition, segmentation and radiomics/DL pipeline applied as described.
probast_rationale: Multi-center cohort with external validation and DeLong comparison; residual overfitting risk from data-driven feature selection.
appraisal_note: Large two-center DLRN with internal+external validation (AUC 0.90-0.94) and SHAP/Grad-CAM interpretability; strongest design in batch.

title: Study on the prediction of postoperative metastasis in renal cancer using perirenal fat CT radiomics combined with clinical features.
rationale_c1: Retrospective single/multi-center recruitment (single-center, n=120); selection bias plausible.
rationale_c2: Radiomics extraction (IBSI-standard) and clinicopathologic/reference-standard outcome measures are appropriate.
rationale_c3: Pathologic/follow-up outcome data reported for included cases.
rationale_c4: Limited confounder adjustment beyond radiomics signature; small sample raises overfitting risk.
rationale_c5: Imaging acquisition, segmentation and radiomics/DL pipeline applied as described.
probast_rationale: Single/limited-center retrospective series with small sample and data-driven radiomics feature selection; overfitting risk.
appraisal_note: Small single-center cohort (n=120); combined-model AUC 0.958 with only 36 metastasis events raises overfitting concern.

title: Machine learning derived proliferating T cell-related signature: a novel biomarker for prognosis and treatment efficacy in clear cell renal cell carcinoma.
rationale_c1: Training cohort from CheckMate025 RCT plus multiple large trial-derived/public validation cohorts (IMmotion151, JAVELIN101, TCGA, WCH).
rationale_c2: Transcriptomic and treatment-response/survival endpoints are standard and matched to aims.
rationale_c3: Multiple large independent cohorts report OS/PFS and treatment-response data.
rationale_c4: 101-algorithm LOOCV screen and median-split risk groups; trial-derived cohorts partially mitigate confounding vs pure convenience samples.
rationale_c5: ML ensemble pipeline and multi-omics (spatial/single-cell) validation applied as described.
criteria_note: MMAT non-randomized (Hong 2018); unusually strong validation via RCT-derived cohorts.
probast_rationale: Validation spans multiple RCT/trial cohorts (CheckMate025, IMmotion151, JAVELIN101) strengthening external validity, but 101-algorithm mining and median-split risk score retain overfitting risk.
appraisal_note: Validation cohorts drawn from immunotherapy RCTs (CheckMate025, IMmotion151, JAVELIN Renal101) is a notable strength versus typical convenience-cohort signatures in this corpus.

title: MRI-based habitat radiomics for predicting WHO/ISUP nuclear grade in clear cell renal cell carcinoma.
rationale_c1: Retrospective single/multi-center recruitment (single-center, n=154 (train/test split)); selection bias plausible.
rationale_c2: Radiomics extraction (IBSI-standard) and clinicopathologic/reference-standard outcome measures are appropriate.
rationale_c3: Pathologic/follow-up outcome data reported for included cases.

rationale_c1: Cohorte de un solo centro (un centro, SMOTE + 5-fold CV), muestra de conveniencia, representatividad limitada.
rationale_c2: Adquisicion de imagen/expresion y extraccion de caracteristicas descritas de forma reproducible.
rationale_c3: N pequeno (n=77 pacientes); no se detalla perdida de seguimiento o datos faltantes de forma exhaustiva.
rationale_c4: Ajuste por confusores limitado o ausente mas alla de las variables incluidas en el nomograma final.
rationale_c5: Estudio retrospectivo de un centro ejecutado segun protocolo declarado, sin aleatorizacion.
probast_rationale: Analisis de textura CT por ML para masas testiculares; balanceo SMOTE por clases desbalanceadas y validacion cruzada interna unicamente, sin cohorte externa.

title: T2-Weighted Image-Based Radiomics Signature for Discriminating Between Seminomas and Nonseminoma.
rationale_c1: Cohorte de un solo centro (un centro, muestra muy pequena), muestra de conveniencia, representatividad limitada.
rationale_c2: Adquisicion de imagen/expresion y extraccion de caracteristicas descritas de forma reproducible.
rationale_c3: N pequeno (n=39 pacientes (19 seminoma/20 no seminoma)); no se detalla perdida de seguimiento o datos faltantes de forma exhaustiva.
rationale_c4: Ajuste por confusores limitado o ausente mas alla de las variables incluidas en el nomograma final.
rationale_c5: Estudio retrospectivo de un centro ejecutado segun protocolo declarado, sin aleatorizacion.
probast_rationale: Firma radiomica T2WI con muestra muy pequena (n=39) y sin validacion externa; alto riesgo de sobreajuste dado el numero de features frente al n.
appraisal_note: Tamano muestral muy pequeno (n=39) con AUC muy alto (0.979), compatible con sobreajuste; interpretar con cautela.

title: Applying Radiomics to Predict Pathology of Postchemotherapy Retroperitoneal Nodal Masses in Germ Cell Tumors.
rationale_c1: Cohorte de un solo centro (un centro, validacion cruzada anidada 10-fold), muestra de conveniencia, representatividad limitada.
rationale_c2: Adquisicion de imagen/expresion y extraccion de caracteristicas descritas de forma reproducible.
rationale_c3: N pequeno (n=77 pacientes, 102 ROIs); no se detalla perdida de seguimiento o datos faltantes de forma exhaustiva.
rationale_c4: Ajuste por confusores limitado o ausente mas alla de las variables incluidas en el nomograma final.
rationale_c5: Estudio retrospectivo de un centro ejecutado segun protocolo declarado, sin aleatorizacion.
probast_rationale: Clasificador SVM radiomica para fibrosis vs tumor viable/teratoma; validacion cruzada anidada interna unicamente, sin cohorte externa independiente.

title: H&E-stained whole slide image deep learning predicts SPOP mutation state in prostate cancer
rationale_c1: The TCGA set is a quality-filtered public subset (177 of 499) and the MSK-IMPACT set is a selected archive, so population representativeness is unclear.
rationale_c2: H&E whole-slide images and sequenced SPOP mutation labels match the stated prediction target.
rationale_c3: Only 20 TCGA and 19 MSK-IMPACT mutants remained after quality control, so outcome completeness for the source cohorts is uncertain.
rationale_c4: The meta-ensemble was tested in both directions between TCGA frozen sections and an independent MSK-IMPACT FFPE cohort.
rationale_c5: The described ensemble, cross-validation, and bootstrap confidence-interval pipeline was applied to both cohorts.
probast_rationale: Public and archived cohorts with very few SPOP-mutant slides, cross-cohort AUROCs, and heavy ensemble mining in a small-data setting.
appraisal_note: This is an unreviewed bioRxiv preprint, and the training procedure is largely deferred to the supplement.

title: Automated tumour budding quantification by machine learning augments TNM staging in muscle-invasive bladder cancer prognosis.
rationale_c1: The cohort is a single-city cystectomy archive reduced from 163 to 100 cases, so representativeness of MIBC is unclear.
rationale_c2: Immunofluorescence whole-slide budding counts and disease-specific survival from the national registry fit the prognostic question.
rationale_c3: Cases with unknown disease-related death or unusable sections were excluded, and the remaining 100 patients have stated follow-up.
rationale_c4: The survival tree uses TNM before tumour-budding count, and leave-one-out runs kept that split in 97 of 100 iterations.
rationale_c5: Automated budding quantification and the classification-and-regression-tree analysis were applied as specified to the full cohort.
probast_rationale: Single-center cystectomy series with a survival tree and hazard ratio, but no external cohort and several budding features screened.

title: Pan-Renal Cell Carcinoma classification and survival prediction from histopathology images using deep learning.
rationale_c1: TCGA whole-slide images are a public convenience sample, and 972 slides were removed for reading or compatibility problems.
rationale_c2: ResNet classification of RCC subtypes and a LASSO Cox model on tumor shape and nuclear features match the diagnostic and survival aims.
rationale_c3: Survival modeling is limited to clear-cell cases with a median-score split, and follow-up completeness is not stated.
rationale_c4: Subtype and survival models use internal splits of the same TCGA slides, with no independent external cohort.
rationale_c5: The reported ResNet, DAG-SVM, and two-level cross-validated Cox pipeline was applied to the downloaded slides.
probast_rationale: TCGA-only histopathology mining with internal splits, class imbalance, and a median risk index for survival.

title: Radiomics and machine learning of multisequence multiparametric prostate MRI: Towards improved non-invasive prostate cancer characterization.
rationale_c1: Sixty-two consecutive prostatectomy patients from one center over about 14 months are a small convenience sample.
rationale_c2: Lesion masks were aligned to whole-mount sections with re-slicing and non-rigid deformation, which the authors flag as unresolved.
rationale_c3: Ten of 72 enrolled patients were excluded for motion, susceptibility artifact, or incomplete data, and the analyzed set is described.
rationale_c4: Performance is estimated only by leave-pair-out cross-validation in the same 62-patient set, without an external cohort.
rationale_c5: Multiparametric MRI and the regularized logistic models were acquired and fit under the stated protocol.
probast_rationale: Small single-center Gleason classifier with pathology-guided MRI contours, many texture features, and internal cross-validation only.
appraisal_note: Regions of interest were matched to prostatectomy, so preoperative lesion localization is not independently tested.

title: Random forest-based modelling to detect biomarkers for prostate cancer progression.
rationale_c1: The discovery set was deliberately restricted to extreme good-prognosis versus poor-prognosis phenotypes, and the external sets are public cohorts.
rationale_c2: Illumina 450k methylation and biochemical-recurrence labels, plus later immunohistochemistry, match the prognostic question.
rationale_c3: Low-quality samples were removed to leave 35 patients in each discovery group, and ICGC and TCGA clinical labels were available for validation.
rationale_c4: The random-forest classifier was tested in ICGC and TCGA-PRAD, and ZIC2 was checked against standard clinicopathological variables in a large tissue microarray.
rationale_c5: Array processing, cell-composition adjustment, and the random-forest training split were carried out as described.
probast_rationale: Extreme-phenotype discovery of 70 cases gave a 95% internal AUC, with lower external AUCs and a loose FDR threshold for CpG selection.
appraisal_note: External AUCs apply the same extreme good-versus-poor definition rather than an unselected clinical spectrum.

title: A CT-based radiomics model to detect prostate cancer lymph node metastases in PSMA radioguided surgery patients.
journal: Eur J Nucl Med Mol Imaging
rationale_c1: Patients are a selected PSMA-radioguided-surgery series, not an unselected population with recurrent prostate cancer.
rationale_c2: Contrast CT radiomic features and histologic lymph-node status are appropriate to the detection question.
rationale_c3: Every analyzed node had histologic confirmation after radioguided resection, and PET-histology mismatches were excluded.
rationale_c4: Texture and shape features were strongly tied to node volume, and the model does not adjust clinical confounders beyond a held-out imaging split.
rationale_c5: In-house versus external CT acquisition, segmentation, and LASSO modeling followed the stated workflow.
probast_rationale: Nodes were chosen from PSMA-positive surgical templates, mismatches were dropped, and the combined model reached a testing AUC of 0.95.
appraisal_note: The testing cohort is external CT acquisition within the same radioguided-surgery pathway, not an unselected staging population.

title: Differentiation of low and high grade renal cell carcinoma on routine MRI with an externally validated automatic machine learning algorithm.
rationale_c1: Lesions were retrospectively assembled from several hospitals plus TCIA only when Fuhrman grade was available.
rationale_c2: Preoperative T2 and contrast T1 radiomics and surgical Fuhrman grade match the low-versus-high-grade question.
rationale_c3: All 482 analyzed lesions had surgical Fuhrman grade, and biopsy-only and ungraded cases were excluded.
rationale_c4: An independent 43-lesion set from a separate institution was held out from training and internal testing.
rationale_c5: Segmentation, IBSI feature extraction, and both the hand-tuned and TPOT pipelines were applied as described.
probast_rationale: Thousands of MRI features and many selector-classifier pairs were searched, and external AUCs were about 0.59 to 0.60.
appraisal_note: External discrimination is near chance, with sensitivity of 0.12 for the best automated pipeline.

title: Integrative multi-omics analysis of muscle-invasive bladder cancer identifies prognostic biomarkers for frontline chemotherapy and immunotherapy.
rationale_c1: Integrative clustering starts from a TCGA muscle-invasive bladder cancer convenience cohort.
rationale_c2: Multi-omics profiles, overall survival, and treatment-response labels are appropriate to the subtype and biomarker aims.
rationale_c3: Only 388 of 412 TCGA cases had complete multi-omics, and chemotherapy detail was unavailable for several external series.
rationale_c4: The 42-gene classifier trained on TCGA was applied to additional expression cohorts, including neoadjuvant and immunotherapy sets.
rationale_c5: iClusterBayes and the k-nearest-neighbor classifier were run with the stated cluster and k settings.
probast_rationale: TCGA multi-omics subtyping with a 42-gene panel and external survival or response tests, after a large feature search.

title: Machine learning-based analysis of [<sup>18</sup>F]DCFPyL PET radiomics for risk stratification in primary prostate cancer.
journal: Eur J Nucl Med Mol Imaging
rationale_c1: Seventy-six consecutive surgical candidates at one center do not establish representativeness of primary prostate cancer.
rationale_c2: Preoperative PSMA PET radiomics and prostatectomy or biopsy outcomes match the risk-stratification aims.
rationale_c3: Only 71 patients underwent surgery, and lymph-node and distant-metastasis events are few, so outcome stability is uncertain.
rationale_c4: Models were assessed only by repeated nested cross-validation, and the authors state that no external dataset was available.
rationale_c5: Prospective PET acquisition, delineation, and within-fold preprocessing were performed as specified.
probast_rationale: Single-center cohort of 76 patients, 480 radiomic features, rare metastatic events, and no external validation.
appraisal_note: Cross-validated AUCs have wide standard deviations, consistent with few lymph-node and metastasis events.

title: Value of radiomics in differential diagnosis of chromophobe renal cell carcinoma and renal oncocytoma.
rationale_c1: Sixty-one pathologically confirmed tumors from one hospital, with only 17 oncocytomas, are a narrow convenience sample.
rationale_c2: Triphasic contrast CT features and surgical histology are appropriate for separating chromophobe carcinoma from oncocytoma.
rationale_c3: Eight patients lacked clinical data and five lacked an excretory phase, so completeness is uncertain in an already small set.
rationale_c4: Five classifiers were compared by five-fold cross-validation in the same sample, with no external cohort or confounder model.
rationale_c5: Manual segmentation, LASSO selection, and the reported classifiers were applied to the institutional scans.
probast_rationale: One thousand twenty-nine CT features were reduced in 61 tumors, and the best cross-validated AUC was 0.964 with 17 oncocytomas.
appraisal_note: A cross-validated AUC of 0.96 in this imbalanced single-center set is an overfitting signal.

title: Computed Tomography Radiomics for Predicting Pathological Grade of Renal Cell Carcinoma.
rationale_c1: Consecutive nephrectomy cases from one hospital remain a single-center retrospective sample.
rationale_c2: Preoperative CT size and density plus texture features, read against re-reviewed ISUP grade, fit the grading question.
rationale_c3: Included patients had pathologic confirmation and preoperative CT, and grade was reassigned by two uropathologists.
rationale_c4: Training and validation are a random 3:1 split of the same center, without external testing or a confounder model.
rationale_c5: CT acquisition, blinded radiologic review, and the combined predictive model were carried out as described.
probast_rationale: Single-center internal split with class imbalance and a combined validation AUC of 0.91, without an external cohort.

title: Computed Tomography-Based Radiomics Model for Predicting the WHO/ISUP Grade of Clear Cell Renal Cell Carcinoma Preoperatively: A Multicenter Study.
rationale_c1: Cases were retrospectively taken from four hospitals over 20 months, mixing resection and biopsy, so representativeness is unclear.
rationale_c2: Corticomedullary and nephrographic CT features and WHO/ISUP grade are appropriate to preoperative grading.
rationale_c3: Each included tumor had pathologic ccRCC grade, and artifact-degraded examinations were excluded.
rationale_c4: The logistic model was tested in 75 patients from three hospitals separate from the 122-patient training hospital.
rationale_c5: Multicenter CT segmentation, mRMR filtering, and stepwise logistic regression followed the stated pipeline.
probast_rationale: External AUC was 0.81, but sensitivity fell from 0.85 to 0.58 and the reference standard mixes resection with biopsy.
appraisal_note: External sensitivity was 0.58, and grade came from either resection or percutaneous biopsy.

title: MRI-Based Grading of Clear Cell Renal Cell Carcinoma Using a Machine Learning Classifier.
rationale_c1: Ninety-nine surgical ccRCC cases from one hospital are a retrospective convenience sample.
rationale_c2: Corticomedullary MRI texture features and histologic ISUP grade are appropriate to the grading task.
rationale_c3: All enrolled tumors were histologically verified, with stated exclusions for artifact, tiny lesions, and prior treatment.
rationale_c4: Hidden-layer size was tuned on the 29-patient validation split, so that split does not independently control optimism.
rationale_c5: Single-reader segmentation, MaZda extraction, and the multilayer perceptron were applied as specified.
probast_rationale: A single two-dimensional slice and validation-set tuning accompanied a training AUC of 0.997 versus 0.758 on validation.
appraisal_note: The number of hidden nodes was chosen to maximize accuracy on the validation set.

title: MRI-based radiomics models to assess prostate cancer, extracapsular extension and positive surgical margins.
rationale_c1: Four hundred fifty-nine patients from one hospital are a retrospective convenience series.
rationale_c2: T2-weighted and ADC radiomics plus clinical variables are appropriate for lesion, ECE, and margin prediction.
rationale_c3: ECE and margin labels were taken from pathology reports without slide re-review, and matching to MRI is acknowledged as uncertain.
rationale_c4: Each target uses a 7:3 split of the same center, without an external cohort.
rationale_c5: Consecutive MRI-biopsy accrual, pyradiomics extraction, and signature fitting followed the stated protocol.
probast_rationale: Single-center internal testing of 851 features for three endpoints, with ECE radiomics AUC as low as 0.625 before clinical variables.

title: MRI-derived radiomics model for baseline prediction of prostate cancer progression on active surveillance.
rationale_c1: This is a single-center case-control sample of 71 active-surveillance patients, not a consecutive inception cohort.
rationale_c2: Baseline T2 and ADC radiomics plus clinicopathological variables match the progression-prediction aim.
rationale_c3: Progression mixes repeat-biopsy upgrade with PRECISE score 5, so the outcome is not uniformly ascertained.
rationale_c4: Models were compared by leave-one-out cross-validation only, with no external cohort.
rationale_c5: The stated MRI protocol, robustness filtering, and cross-validated model grid were applied to the included lesions.
probast_rationale: Case-control sampling of 73 lesions, a composite progression label, and leave-one-out testing without an external set.
appraisal_note: Ten of 35 progression events were radiological PRECISE score 5 rather than biopsy upgrade.

title: Machine learning-based CT radiomics approach for predicting WHO/ISUP nuclear grade of clear cell renal cell carcinoma: an exploratory and comparative study.
rationale_c1: Four hundred six nephrectomy cases from one institution remain a retrospective single-center sample.
rationale_c2: Nephrographic-phase CT radiomics and re-reviewed WHO/ISUP grade are appropriate to preoperative grading.
rationale_c3: Exclusions for non-ISUP grading, missing phases, artifacts, and prior therapy are stated, and included cases have surgical grade.
rationale_c4: Training, validation, and testing cohorts are internal partitions, and high-grade cases were oversampled with SMOTE.
rationale_c5: Single-scanner CT, blinded semantic reads, and the SVM feature-selection comparison followed the protocol.
probast_rationale: Single-institution internal testing with SMOTE for the minority high-grade class and three feature-selection algorithms.

title: Magnetic resonance imaging-based radiomics signature for preoperative prediction of Ki67 expression in bladder cancer.
rationale_c1: One hundred seventy-nine bladder-cancer cases from one center are a retrospective convenience sample.
rationale_c2: T2-weighted and DCE radiomics are appropriate for a preoperative call of immunohistochemical Ki67 status.
rationale_c3: Inclusion required Ki67 immunohistochemistry and prognostic information, and 33 patients failing criteria were excluded.
rationale_c4: The 7:3 split is internal, and SMOTE balanced the training set without an external cohort.
rationale_c5: MRI segmentation, pyradiomics extraction, and the SVM and LASSO signatures were built as described.
probast_rationale: Ki67 was imbalanced about 1 to 3.8, SMOTE was applied in training, and validation remained an internal split.
appraisal_note: The model predicts Ki67 immunohistochemistry, and disease-free survival is reported only for that predicted label.

title: Robust Prognostic Subtyping of Muscle-Invasive Bladder Cancer Revealed by Deep Learning-Based Multi-Omics Data Integration.
rationale_c1: Subtyping uses TCGA muscle-invasive bladder cancers, a public convenience cohort.
rationale_c2: Copy number, expression, miRNA, and methylation inputs with overall survival match the prognostic-subtyping aim.
rationale_c3: Only stage II–IV samples with prognostic information were kept, and completeness of survival follow-up is not quantified.
rationale_c4: Expression classifiers were checked on an internal hold-out and on three GEO microarray cohorts with survival separation.
rationale_c5: The autoencoder, Cox feature filter, and k-means clustering were run with the stated architecture.
probast_rationale: Autoencoder features were filtered by univariate Cox association with survival in the same TCGA samples before clustering.
appraisal_note: Subtype labels depend on survival-associated features from the same TCGA samples used to claim prognostic separation.

title: A CT-based radiomics model for predicting renal capsule invasion in renal cell carcinoma.
rationale_c1: One hundred twenty-six RCC patients from one cancer hospital are a retrospective convenience sample.
rationale_c2: Preoperative multiphase CT features and pathology re-review of capsule invasion match the prediction target.
rationale_c3: Included patients had complete preoperative CT and postsurgical pathology, including capsule status.
rationale_c4: Performance is five-fold cross-validation only, with no external cohort or clinical confounder model.
rationale_c5: Three-phase CT segmentation and the five classifiers were applied as specified.
probast_rationale: Small single-center set, two-dimensional contours, five classifiers, and cross-validation without a held-out external cohort.

title: An Ultrasonic-Based Radiomics Nomogram for Distinguishing Between Benign and Malignant Solid Renal Masses.
rationale_c1: Malignant masses were randomly downsampled from 1,777 to 442 to balance benign lesions, so the sample is not representative.
rationale_c2: Preoperative ultrasound radiomics and surgical pathology are appropriate for benign-versus-malignant classification.
rationale_c3: Included masses had usable ultrasound and complete clinicopathology after stated exclusions.
rationale_c4: Training and validation are a random internal split after artificial class balancing, without an external cohort.
rationale_c5: Ultrasound segmentation, RadScore construction, and the clinical nomogram were applied as described.
probast_rationale: Benign and malignant prevalence was engineered by undersampling cancers, and validation is an internal 480/120 split.
appraisal_note: Malignant lesions were randomly undersampled so the modeled prevalence does not match the source case mix.

title: Application Value of Radiomic Nomogram in the Differential Diagnosis of Prostate Cancer and Hyperplasia.
rationale_c1: One hundred forty-six patients imaged at one hospital are a retrospective convenience sample.
rationale_c2: T2-weighted radiomic features and biopsy or prostatectomy diagnoses are appropriate for separating cancer from hyperplasia.
rationale_c3: Patients without pathology, with prior treatment, or with undelineable lesions were excluded, and the analyzed set is fully labeled.
rationale_c4: The nomogram combines the radiomic score with PSA, an independent clinical factor, in a multivariable logistic model.
rationale_c5: ITK-SNAP segmentation, LASSO selection, and nomogram fitting followed the stated workflow.
probast_rationale: The nomogram testing AUC of 0.90 comes from a 7:3 internal split of 146 single-center cases.
appraisal_note: PSA is in the nomogram, but the test set is an internal split from the same hospital.

title: Evaluation of the Efficiency of MRI-Based Radiomics Classifiers in the Diagnosis of Prostate Lesions.
rationale_c1: Two hundred thirty-eight patients from one hospital, drawn from 872 MRI examinations, are a retrospective convenience sample.
rationale_c2: ADC, DWI, and T2 radiomics compared with biopsy or prostatectomy pathology match the diagnostic question.
rationale_c3: Included patients had post-MRI pathology, and incomplete sequences, undelineable lesions, and artifacts were excluded.
rationale_c4: The 142/96 split is random within one institution, and several classifiers were screened without external testing.
rationale_c5: Normalization, pyradiomics extraction, and the six classifiers were applied as described.
probast_rationale: Six classifiers were compared on one internal split, and the lesion-based random-forest AUC reached 0.931.
appraisal_note: The independent test set is a random split of the same institution, and the highest AUC is lesion-based.

title: Feasibility Study on Predicting Recurrence Risk of Bladder Cancer Based on Radiomics Features of Multiphase CT Images.
rationale_c1: One hundred eighty-three surgical bladder-cancer patients from one hospital are a retrospective convenience sample.
rationale_c2: Multiphase CT radiomics and cystoscopic-pathologic recurrence within two years match the prognostic question.
rationale_c3: Follow-up cystoscopy and imaging define recurrence, and patients with incomplete clinicopathology or unusable CT were excluded.
rationale_c4: Cox models retained tumor number, grade, and the radiomics score as independent predictors of recurrence.
rationale_c5: CT segmentation, logistic radiomics models, and the combined Cox model were applied as specified.
probast_rationale: The combined model uses an internal 7:3 split, and phase-specific radiomic models were screened before the clinical combination.

title: Multiparametric MRI and Machine Learning Based Radiomic Models for Preoperative Prediction of Multiple Biological Characteristics in Prostate Cancer.
rationale_c1: Two hundred fifty-two prostatectomy patients from one hospital are a retrospective convenience sample.
rationale_c2: Multiparametric MRI radiomics and prostatectomy pathology or immunohistochemistry match the five biological targets.
rationale_c3: Several candidate markers were dropped for incomplete data, so completeness across biological endpoints is uncertain.
rationale_c4: Each endpoint uses a 4:1 internal split, and six classifiers were compared without an external cohort.
rationale_c5: Manual VOI transfer across sequences, mRMR, and recursive feature elimination were applied as described.
probast_rationale: Five endpoints and six classifiers were screened on 5,343 features from one single-center split.
appraisal_note: Ki67, S100, extracapsular extension, perineural invasion, and surgical margin were each modeled separately on the same cohort.

title: Predictive radiomics signature for treatment response to nivolumab in patients with advanced renal cell carcinoma.
rationale_c1: Twenty-seven patients treated with nivolumab at one institution are too selected to represent metastatic RCC.
rationale_c2: Pretreatment and first post-treatment CT texture features address the response-classification question as framed.
rationale_c3: Ten of 37 identified patients were excluded for missing or incompatible CT, and labels are lesion-level rather than patient-level.
rationale_c4: The support-vector classifier was assessed only by nested cross-validation in 27 patients, with no external cohort.
rationale_c5: Lesion contouring, grey-level quantization, and LibSVM training followed the stated settings.
probast_rationale: Response counts durable stable disease and treatment beyond progression as response, and one classifier uses the post-treatment scan.
appraisal_note: Accuracy was 69% and 66% in 27 patients, using a nonstandard response label at lesion level.

title: Prostate cancer therapy personalization via multi-modal deep learning on randomized phase III clinical trials.
rationale_c1: Slides were available for 5,654 of 7,764 randomized patients, and the validation subset was constrained to a target NCCN AUC band.
rationale_c2: Baseline clinical variables and pretreatment biopsy slides are appropriate inputs for the long-term trial endpoints.
rationale_c3: The source trials report a median follow-up of 11.4 years for distant metastasis, biochemical failure, and survival.
rationale_c4: Clinical covariates are in the model, but the 80/20 split pools five trials and the test set was chosen so the NCCN AUC sat between 0.70 and 0.75.
rationale_c5: Digitization, self-supervised pretraining, and fusion modeling were applied to the anonymized trial data as described.
probast_rationale: A large multi-trial development set still uses an internal split whose test cases were selected to place NCCN discrimination in a preset AUC range.
appraisal_note: The held-out set was selected so the NCCN 5-year distant-metastasis AUC fell between 0.70 and 0.75.

title: A multi-model based on radiogenomics and deep learning techniques associated with histological grade and survival in clear cell renal cell carcinoma.
rationale_c1: The cohort is a convenience subset of public TCGA/TCIA ccRCC cases, so population representativeness is unclear.
rationale_c2: Nephrographic CT radiomics, deep-learning features, and RNA-seq were paired with pathological grade and survival.
rationale_c3: Inclusion required complete genetic and clinical information, and grade was available for the 177 analyzed patients.
rationale_c4: Grade was predicted from a random 8:2 split of one public cohort without adjustment for stage, which differed by grade.
rationale_c5: Blinded segmentation, ICC filtering, and the stated LASSO workflow were followed.
probast_rationale: Public TCIA cases, a small internal test set of 35, and high-dimensional radiomic, deep-learning, and transcriptomic features leave a high risk of optimistic performance.
appraisal_note: Grade and survival models were fit on one TCIA cohort with an internal split, and transcriptomic features come from the same tumors that define histological grade.

title: Comparison and analysis of multiple machine learning models for discriminating benign and malignant testicular lesions based on magnetic resonance imaging radiomics.
rationale_c1: This is a single-center retrospective series of 115 operated or biopsied testicular lesions, so representativeness is unclear.
rationale_c2: T2-weighted MRI radiomics and postoperative or biopsy histology are appropriate for benign-versus-malignant classification.
rationale_c3: Every included lesion had a pathology diagnosis after documented exclusions for missing images or absent histology.
rationale_c4: Classifiers used radiomics alone and did not account for the age difference between benign and malignant lesions.
rationale_c5: A fixed MRI protocol, ICC filtering, and the stated PyRadiomics workflow were applied.
probast_rationale: Ten algorithms were compared on 1,781 features in a small single-center 70/30 split, and the reported winner was the model with the highest test AUC.
appraisal_note: The preferred XGBoost model was selected by test-set AUC among ten classifiers rather than locked before the hold-out evaluation.

title: Deep learning and radiomic feature-based blending ensemble classifier for malignancy risk prediction in cystic renal lesions.
rationale_c1: Both cohorts are retrospective pathology-confirmed surgical series, so spectrum and referral bias remain unclear.
rationale_c2: Arterial-phase CT radiomics and 3D-ResNet features were compared with histopathology as the reference standard.
rationale_c3: Every enrolled cystic lesion had a final pathological diagnosis in the development and testing cohorts.
rationale_c4: A separate hospital testing cohort provides an external check on the development model.
rationale_c5: IBSI-oriented extraction, ICC filtering, and ComBat harmonization followed the stated pipeline.
probast_rationale: External AUC was 0.934, but the model was built from 1,231 radiomic plus 2,048 deep features and the external set contained only 10 malignant lesions.
appraisal_note: The external test cohort was highly imbalanced, with 10 malignant and 53 benign cystic lesions.

title: Interpretability of radiomics models is improved when using feature group selection strategies for predicting molecular and clinical targets in clear-cell renal cell carcinoma: insights from the TRACERx Renal study.
rationale_c1: Only the first 101 TRACERx Renal recruits, reduced to 91 lesions, were imaged, so representativeness of ccRCC is unclear.
rationale_c2: Pre-surgical contrast CT radiomics were used to classify prespecified histological and genomic targets.
rationale_c3: Class counts differ across 20 targets, and some continuous targets were median-binarized, so outcome completeness is unclear.
rationale_c4: Performance rests on nested cross-validation in one small cohort without confounder adjustment or an external sample.
rationale_c5: The prospective TRACERx imaging and segmentation protocol was applied as described.
probast_rationale: Ninety-one lesions were used to screen many radiomic pipelines against 20 targets, with nested cross-validation only and median splits for some endpoints.
appraisal_note: Several molecular targets were median-binarized inside this small single-trial sample, and there is no external cohort.

title: Magnetic resonance imaging radiomics-based prediction of clinically significant prostate cancer in equivocal PI-RADS 3 lesions in the transitional zone.
rationale_c1: Men with PI-RADS 3 transition-zone lesions from two hospitals are a selected biopsy population.
rationale_c2: T2 and ADC radiomics plus PSAD and mean ADC were compared with biopsy grade group.
rationale_c3: All 243 included men had a biopsy result classifying csPCa versus no csPCa.
rationale_c4: Multivariable logistic models retained PSAD and mean ADC alongside the radiomic signature.
rationale_c5: Blinded PI-RADS reading and the stated segmentation and LASSO workflow were followed.
probast_rationale: Only 30 csPCa events were available, the two hospitals were pooled and randomly split, and biopsy rather than prostatectomy was the reference.
appraisal_note: The bi-institutional data were randomly split rather than held out by center, and the authors note biopsy bias with only 30 csPCa cases.

title: Predicting prostate cancer in men with PSA levels of 4-10 ng/mL: MRI-based radiomics can help junior radiologists improve the diagnostic performance.
rationale_c1: A single-hospital retrospective series restricted to PSA 4–10 ng/mL and PI-RADS ≥3 is not clearly population-representative.
rationale_c2: Multiparametric MRI radiomics and blinded PI-RADS scores were compared with biopsy or prostatectomy histology.
rationale_c3: Patients lacking clinical or pathological data were excluded, and the 171 analyzed men had histology.
rationale_c4: The radiomics logistic model did not adjust for age or lesion zone, which differed between cancer and non-cancer.
rationale_c5: Readers were blinded, and segmentation and feature extraction followed the stated GE workflow.
probast_rationale: A single-center time split produced nearly identical AUCs of 0.932 and 0.922 from high-dimensional MRI radiomics.
appraisal_note: Training and testing AUCs remained above 0.92 on one hospital's temporal split, which is a strong optimism signal.

title: Prediction of prostate tumour hypoxia using pre-treatment MRI-derived radiomics: preliminary findings.
rationale_c1: Consecutive patients from two radiotherapy centers over 2007–2013 remain a selected historical cohort.
rationale_c2: Whole-prostate T2 radiomics were compared with a prespecified biopsy hypoxia gene signature.
rationale_c3: Inclusion required pre-treatment MRI, the hypoxia signature, and the listed clinical variables.
rationale_c4: Age, ISUP grade, PSA, and T stage were offered to the classifiers together with radiomic features.
rationale_c5: CLAIM-oriented segmentation, histogram standardization, and repeated cross-validation were applied as described.
probast_rationale: Many classifier and feature-selection combinations were tuned on a pooled 80:20 split, and the best test AUC was 0.69 with a very wide interval.
appraisal_note: The two centers were pooled into one split, and hypoxia was a gene-signature proxy whose radiomic model was not significantly better than clinical variables.

title: The value of a dual-energy CT Iodine map radiomics model for the prediction of collagen fiber content in the ccRCC tumor microenvironment.
rationale_c1: Eighty-seven consecutive surgical ccRCC cases from one hospital are a small convenience sample.
rationale_c2: Collagen was dichotomized by one pathologist at a visual half-field threshold, so measurement adequacy is unclear.
rationale_c3: All 87 included patients had both preoperative dual-energy CT and a Masson collagen reading.
rationale_c4: The radiomic classifiers did not adjust for age and tumor diameter, which were associated with collagen content.
rationale_c5: The dual-energy CT protocol, ICC filtering, and Radcloud workflow were applied as described.
probast_rationale: Six classifiers on a 60/27 split reached training AUCs of 0.997–1.0 while validation AUCs fell to about 0.70 against a subjective collagen label.
appraisal_note: The predicted endpoint is a subjective histologic collagen split rather than a clinical diagnosis or survival outcome.

title: Value of handcrafted and deep radiomic features towards training robust machine learning classifiers for prediction of prostate cancer disease aggressiveness.
rationale_c1: PROSTATEx is a single-center public challenge set, not a defined clinical population sample.
rationale_c2: Whole-gland T2, DWI, and ADC radiomics and deep features were used to classify biopsy-defined significant cancer.
rationale_c3: Challenge labels were available for the 181 patients retained after segmentation exclusions.
rationale_c4: Models were radiomics classifiers on one public cohort without clinical confounder adjustment or an external cohort.
rationale_c5: PyRadiomics settings, ICC checks, and the compared mask-sampling strategies were applied as specified.
probast_rationale: More than 3,000 features and several segmentation strategies were compared with hold-out testing inside one public dataset.
appraisal_note: All development and hold-out testing used the same public PROSTATEx cohort.

title: A nomogram based on peripheral lymphocyte for predicting 8-year survival in patients with prostate cancer: a single-center study using LASSO-cox regression.
rationale_c1: Ninety-four men aged at least 60 from one Chinese registry over two decades are a narrow convenience sample.
rationale_c2: Peripheral lymphocyte subsets, age, and T stage were modeled against all-cause overall survival.
rationale_c3: Patients without survival time and status were excluded, so the OS endpoint is complete in the analyzed 94.
rationale_c4: LASSO-Cox and backward multivariable selection retained age, T stage, and lymphocyte measures.
rationale_c5: Flow-cytometry and the stated LASSO-Cox nomogram procedure were applied as described.
probast_rationale: Cut-points were chosen with X-tile on the outcome in 94 patients, and discrimination was estimated without an external cohort.
appraisal_note: Lymphocyte thresholds were outcome-derived with X-tile in the same 94-patient sample used to report the nomogram.

title: A radiomics-based interpretable machine learning model to predict the HER2 status in bladder cancer: a multicenter study.
rationale_c1: Surgical bladder-cancer cases from four hospitals remain a retrospective operative series.
rationale_c2: Nephrographic CT radiomics were compared with blinded IHC HER2 scores on resection specimens.
rationale_c3: Included patients had preoperative CT and a pathological HER2 score after exclusions for missing imaging.
rationale_c4: A 53-patient test set was drawn from three hospitals other than the training center.
rationale_c5: Blinded segmentation, ICC filtering, and the TRIPOD-oriented pipeline were followed.
probast_rationale: Eleven features were chosen from 1,218 and the best of five classifiers was reported, while HER2 2+ was labeled positive without in situ hybridization.
appraisal_note: HER2-positive status grouped IHC 2+ with 3+ without confirmatory ISH, and the reported model was the best of five classifiers.

title: An Integrated Machine Learning Framework Identifies Prognostic Gene Pair Biomarkers Associated with Programmed Cell Death Modalities in Clear Cell Renal Cell Carcinoma.
rationale_c1: TCGA-KIRC and E-MTAB-1980 are public convenience cohorts rather than a population sample.
rationale_c2: Programmed-cell-death gene-pair scores and a CT radiomic score were tied to survival and to the score itself.
rationale_c3: TCGA cases lacking essential clinicopathological annotation were excluded before modeling 518 patients.
rationale_c4: The gene-pair score was tested in an external ArrayExpress cohort and compared with published signatures.
rationale_c5: The ssGSEA, gene-pair, and 10-fold machine-learning procedure was applied as specified.
probast_rationale: One hundred thirteen algorithm combinations were ranked by mean C-index that included the external cohort, and risk groups used a median split.
appraisal_note: The final LASSO plus random-forest model was chosen after comparing 113 combinations on external C-index.

title: Assessing muscle invasion in bladder cancer via virtual biopsy: a study on quantitative parameters and classical radiomics features from dual-energy CT imaging.
rationale_c1: A single-hospital retrospective dual-energy CT urography series is a convenience surgical sample.
rationale_c2: Iodine concentration and venous-phase radiomics were compared with pathological muscle invasion.
rationale_c3: Patients with incomplete imaging or pathology were excluded, leaving 126 with a muscle-invasion label.
rationale_c4: Normalized iodine concentration was an independent factor and was fused with the radiomic model.
rationale_c5: Blinded measurements, consensus segmentation, and the stated SVM pipeline were followed.
probast_rationale: Multiple virtual-monoenergetic radiomic models were selected on a random 7:3 split with only 38 test patients.

title: Clinical application of machine learning models in patients with prostate cancer before prostatectomy.
rationale_c1: Discovery cases came from one prostatectomy practice, and the external scans were still a referred surgical series.
rationale_c2: Clinical, semantic, and T2 radiomic features were compared with prostatectomy extracapsular extension.
rationale_c3: Included men had biopsy-proven cancer, PI-RADS >2 MRI, and a prostatectomy ECE reading.
rationale_c4: Every model included routine clinical variables, and a 55-patient multi-institution set was used for testing.
rationale_c5: ICC filtering and the stated radiomic and semantic workflow were applied to both datasets.
probast_rationale: External images came from 15 sites, but the same radiologist segmented them and the external sample was only 55 men.
appraisal_note: External MRI examinations were interpreted and segmented by the same radiologist who read the discovery set.

title: Comparison in prostate cancer diagnosis with PSA 4-10 ng/mL: radiomics-based model VS. PI-RADS v2.1.
rationale_c1: A single-center retrospective PSA gray-zone biopsy series is not clearly representative of that clinical population.
rationale_c2: ADC and T2 radiomics were compared with targeted or systematic biopsy and with PI-RADS v2.1.
rationale_c3: Patients with incomplete clinical data or pathology-MRI mismatch were excluded, and all 221 had histology.
rationale_c4: The ADC, T2, and combined models used imaging features only, without clinical confounder adjustment.
rationale_c5: Blinded PI-RADS scoring and the stated LASSO logistic workflow were followed.
probast_rationale: Combined-model AUC was 0.979 in training and 0.959 in a random internal split after selection from 851 features per sequence.
appraisal_note: Discrimination barely fell from training to the internal validation split, which suggests overfitting.

title: Contrast-enhanced computed tomography-based radiomics nomogram for predicting HER2 status in urothelial bladder carcinoma.
rationale_c1: One hospital's 2022–2023 operative urothelial carcinoma series is a small convenience sample.
rationale_c2: Corticomedullary CT radiomics plus clinical factors were compared with IHC HER2 on the resection.
rationale_c3: Inclusion required preoperative CT, complete clinical data, and an IHC HER2 result.
rationale_c4: Univariate and multivariate analyses identified clinical predictors that were fused with the radiomic signature.
rationale_c5: Resampling and the One-key AI extraction and modeling workflow were applied as described.
probast_rationale: Eight classifiers were compared and the best was reported on a 24-patient test set, with IHC 2+ counted as HER2-positive.
appraisal_note: The test set had 24 patients, and HER2-positive status combined IHC 2+ and 3+ without ISH.

title: Interpretable machine learning model for predicting clinically significant prostate cancer: integrating intratumoral and peritumoral radiomics with clinical and metabolic features.
rationale_c1: All patients came from one institution's biopsy practice, so representativeness beyond that pathway is unclear.
rationale_c2: Intratumoral and peritumoral MRI radiomics, PI-RADS, PSAD, and MRS were compared with biopsy Gleason score.
rationale_c3: Inclusion required a post-MRI biopsy, and men without biopsy or with incomplete data were excluded.
rationale_c4: The combined XGBoost model included clinicoradiological and metabolic predictors with the radiomic scores.
rationale_c5: Reproducibility segmentation on 30 cases and the stated RFE and XGBoost workflow were followed.
probast_rationale: Reported AUCs were 0.968 in the internal test set and 0.940 in a later single-center temporal set after high-dimensional radiomic selection.
appraisal_note: Both the random test AUC of 0.968 and the same-center temporal AUC of 0.940 are unusually high for biopsy-referenced csPCa.
