title: Machine learning based on radiomics features combing B-mode transrectal ultrasound and contrast-enhanced ultrasound to improve peripheral zone prostate cancer detection.
rationale_c1: Prospectively enrolled men were limited to one hospital and to suspicious peripheral-zone lesions.
rationale_c2: B-mode and CEUS radiomics plus PSA and perfusion measures were compared with targeted biopsy.
rationale_c3: Inclusion required a satisfactory targeted biopsy, and incomplete examinations were excluded.
rationale_c4: Multivariable logistic models identified age, PSAD, total PSA, and rise time as predictors with the radiomic signatures.
rationale_c5: A written consent protocol and a fixed ultrasound, CEUS, and biopsy workflow were followed.
probast_rationale: Thirty-two features were kept from 3,306 in 166 single-center lesions, with validation AUC 0.89 and no external cohort.

title: Machine learning pipeline to analyze clinical and proteomics data: experiences on a prostate cancer case.
rationale_c1: Serum and urine samples from one two-year project are a convenience case set of PCa versus BPH.
rationale_c2: Mass-spectrometry peptides plus PSA and gland size were used to classify biopsy-defined PCa versus BPH.
rationale_c3: Missing clinical values were dropped or mean-imputed, including by diagnostic subset, so completeness is unclear.
rationale_c4: Clinical analytes were entered with the peptide features in the classification pipeline.
rationale_c5: The documented preprocessing, feature-selection, and voting pipeline was applied to both datasets.
probast_rationale: About 1,670 peptides were screened with five selectors and performance was averaged over 10-fold cross-validation only.
appraisal_note: Some missing predictors were replaced by the mean of the same diagnostic class before cross-validation.

title: Multi-sequence MRI-based radiomics model to preoperatively predict the WHO/ISUP grade of clear Cell Renal Cell Carcinoma: a two-center study.
rationale_c1: Surgical ccRCC cases from two hospitals are retrospective convenience samples.
rationale_c2: Multi-sequence MRI radiomics and semantic MRI features were compared with WHO/ISUP grade.
rationale_c3: Cases without a clear WHO/ISUP grade or incomplete target sequences were excluded.
rationale_c4: Intratumoral vessels remained an independent predictor and were combined with the radiomic score, with a separate-center test set.
rationale_c5: Blinded radiological review and the stated segmentation and modeling workflow were followed.
probast_rationale: Seven classifiers were compared on multi-sequence features, and the authors note grade imbalance that limited confounder control.
appraisal_note: The authors report that grade imbalance limited confounder adjustment and may have biased associations.

title: Optimizing radiomics for prostate cancer diagnosis: feature selection strategies, machine learning classifiers, and MRI sequences.
rationale_c1: ProstateNET is a selected multi-center imaging collection and ProstateX2 is a public challenge set.
rationale_c2: T2 and ADC radiomics were used to classify histologically defined Gleason grade group ≥2 cancer.
rationale_c3: csPCa labels from biopsy or prostatectomy were available for both modeled cohorts.
rationale_c4: Models developed on ProstateNET were evaluated on the separate ProstateX2 cohort.
rationale_c5: PyRadiomics preprocessing and the nested comparison of selectors and classifiers were applied as specified.
probast_rationale: Four hundred eighty model variants were compared, and csPCa prevalence shifted from 74% in development to 25% externally.
appraisal_note: csPCa prevalence differed sharply between ProstateNET and ProstateX2, and hundreds of model variants were compared.

title: Predicting first-line VEGFR-TKI resistance and survival in metastatic clear cell renal cell carcinoma using a clinical-radiomic nomogram.
rationale_c1: A single cancer-hospital retrospective series of metastatic ccRCC treated with VEGFR-TKI is a selected sample.
rationale_c2: Baseline CT radiomics and clinical factors were compared with RECIST early progression, PFS, and OS.
rationale_c3: The authors state that some clinical and pathological fields remained incomplete and later therapy affects survival.
rationale_c4: The nomogram combined the radiomic score with clinical factors, and Cox models tested PFS and OS.
rationale_c5: MDT response review and the stated LASSO radiomic workflow were applied.
probast_rationale: The nomogram was split inside one center of 110 patients, including only five IMDC favorable-risk cases.
appraisal_note: Training and test sets were an internal split, and IMDC favorable-risk disease was almost absent.

title: Prediction of clear cell renal cell carcinoma ≤ 4cm: visual assessment of ultrasound characteristics versus ultrasonographic radiomics analysis.
rationale_c1: Operated small renal masses from three Tianjin hospitals remain a surgical convenience sample.
rationale_c2: Clinical ultrasound features and ultrasonographic radiomics were compared with postoperative ccRCC versus angiomyolipoma.
rationale_c3: Inclusion required pathology and adequate ultrasound, and incomplete cases were excluded.
rationale_c4: A comprehensive model combined clinical ultrasound features with radiomics and was tested in an independent two-hospital cohort.
rationale_c5: ITK-SNAP segmentation, PyRadiomics, and the random-forest workflow were applied as described.
probast_rationale: Nine features were selected from 491, and external AUC for the comprehensive model was 0.90 in 69 patients.

title: Prediction of prostate cancer aggressiveness using magnetic resonance imaging radiomics: a dual-center study.
rationale_c1: Biopsy-proven prostate-cancer cases from two hospitals are a retrospective referred sample.
rationale_c2: Small-FOV T2 and delayed post-contrast radiomics were compared with systematic-biopsy Gleason score and positive cores.
rationale_c3: Inclusion required a 12-core biopsy within one month of MRI, and incomplete cases were excluded.
rationale_c4: Separate internal and external validation sets were reported for both aggressiveness endpoints.
rationale_c5: The stated ANOVA, recursive feature elimination, and logistic-regression workflow was followed.
probast_rationale: Radiomics-only models were chosen among several classifiers, and Gleason AUC fell from about 0.81 internally to 0.72 externally.
appraisal_note: Pathology was not centrally reviewed across the two hospitals, and the external Gleason AUC dropped to 0.717.

title: Radiomics predicts the prognosis of patients with clear cell renal cell carcinoma by reflecting the tumor heterogeneity and microenvironment.
rationale_c1: Three hospitals were pooled and a public TCIA/TCGA subset was added, so the sample is not population-based.
rationale_c2: Contrast-CT deep-learning radiomics and clinicopathology were modeled against overall survival.
rationale_c3: Inclusion required complete clinicopathological data, follow-up, and contrast CT.
rationale_c4: Multivariate Cox regression retained the deep-learning score with clinicopathological factors, and TCIA performance was reported.
rationale_c5: The stated segmentation, LASSO, and SHAP workflow was applied to the pooled cohort.
probast_rationale: Thousands of deep radiomic features and an outcome-derived risk cutoff were used, and the institutional test set was a random 7:3 split of pooled hospitals.
appraisal_note: The three hospitals were randomly split rather than separated by center, with TCIA used as a further external check.

title: The value of radiomics based on 2-[18 F]FDG PET/CT in predicting WHO/ISUP grade of clear cell renal cell carcinoma.
rationale_c1: A single-hospital retrospective PET/CT series of surgical ccRCC is a convenience sample.
rationale_c2: FDG PET/CT radiomics and clinical metabolic measures were compared with WHO/ISUP grade.
rationale_c3: Cases without a reported WHO/ISUP grade or with incomplete clinical data were excluded.
rationale_c4: A clinical model was built and then combined with the selected PET radiomic model.
rationale_c5: mRMR, LASSO, and the stated SUV-threshold segmentation workflow were applied.
probast_rationale: Several SUV thresholds and models were compared on a single-center 7:3 split, and the combined AUC was 0.916 in both training and testing.
appraisal_note: The combined model AUC was identical at 0.916 in the training and internal testing splits.

title: Ultrasound-based deep learning radiomics nomogram for risk stratification of testicular masses: a two-center study.
rationale_c1: A retrospective two-hospital ultrasound series of operated testicular lesions is a convenience sample with image-quality exclusions.
rationale_c2: Preoperative ultrasound radiomics and deep-learning features were paired with postoperative pathology for tumor and malignancy labels.
rationale_c3: All 275 included lesions had a definitive postoperative pathological diagnosis.
rationale_c4: The CDLR nomogram combined the deep-learning radiomics signature with a multivariable clinical signature.
rationale_c5: Manual ROIs were drawn blinded to pathology, with intra- and inter-reader ICC checks, and features were extracted with PyRadiomics.
probast_rationale: Center 2 was held out, but high-dimensional ultrasound features and a training AUC of 0.954 leave a high risk of optimism.

title: Using apparent diffusion coefficient maps and radiomics to predict pathological grade in upper urinary tract urothelial carcinoma.
rationale_c1: This single-center retrospective UTUC series excluded artifacts and incomplete records, so representativeness of all UTUC is unclear.
rationale_c2: ADC-map radiomics and mean ADC were compared with post-nephroureterectomy grade as the reference standard.
rationale_c3: Grade was available for all 215 analyzed patients after the stated exclusions.
rationale_c4: The gradient-boosting model used two radiomic features only, without adjustment for clinical confounders, after upsampling the minority class.
rationale_c5: Tumors were segmented on ADC with senior review and an intra-observer ICC check before PyRadiomics extraction.
probast_rationale: A random 7:3 split, eight scanners, mixed b-values, and a training AUC of 1.000 indicate overfitting despite a test AUC of 0.786.
appraisal_note: Training AUC of 1.000 after upsampling is an overfitting signal on a single-center split.

title: A Robust [<sup>18</sup>F]-PSMA-1007 Radiomics Ensemble Model for Prostate Cancer Risk Stratification.
rationale_c1: Only 143 of 832 PET/CT examinations at one hospital met inclusion rules, so the sample is a selected convenience cohort.
rationale_c2: Risk labels came from biopsy Gleason score, and PET-positive lesions were defined by reader judgment rather than prostatectomy histology.
rationale_c3: Gleason category was available for every included patient by design.
rationale_c4: The ensemble used radiomic features alone, with no clinical covariates and with several classifiers screened over 30 iterations.
rationale_c5: IBSI-compliant PyRadiomics features were extracted from manual VOIs using a prespecified iterated LASSO pipeline.
probast_rationale: Single-center biopsy labels, two scanners, 1781 features, and no external test set leave outcome and analysis at elevated risk.
appraisal_note: Authors state there is no external test set and that biopsy, not prostatectomy, was the reference standard.

title: A multi-modal deep learning framework for predicting PSA progression-free survival in metastatic prostate cancer using PSMA PET/CT imaging
rationale_c1: Ninety-nine metastatic prostate cancer patients from one academic center are a small convenience cohort.
rationale_c2: PSMA PET/CT lesion crops plus chart-reviewed clinical variables were aligned to a defined PSA progression-free survival endpoint.
rationale_c3: Only 21.2% of patients had a PSA progression event and completeness of follow-up beyond a 22.4-month median is not shown.
rationale_c4: Twelve clinical variables chosen by LASSO Cox were fused with the imaging network.
rationale_c5: Resampling, lesion cropping, augmentation, and ResNet-Cox training with five-fold cross-validation followed the stated pipeline.
probast_rationale: Five-fold C-indices of 0.75 to 0.94 in about 21 events, with event oversampling, indicate a high risk of overfitting.
appraisal_note: This is an unreviewed preprint with internal cross-validation only and very few PSA-progression events.

title: A novel MRI-based habitat analysis and deep learning for predicting perineural invasion in prostate cancer: a two-center study.
rationale_c1: A retrospective two-center prostatectomy-or-biopsy series can reflect referral and image-availability bias.
rationale_c2: Habitat deep-learning features from T2WI, DWI, and ADC were used to predict pathology-defined perineural invasion.
rationale_c3: Included patients were required to have perineural-invasion pathology and usable clinical and imaging data.
rationale_c4: A clinical model was built and then combined with habitat radscores.
rationale_c5: Images were registered, resampled, and segmented in ITK-SNAP under a described deep-learning workflow.
probast_rationale: Center 2 was external, but the combined model reached a training AUC of 0.999, which is not credible without overfit.
appraisal_note: Combined-model training AUC of 0.999 with sensitivity 1.0 is an overfitting signal despite external habitat AUCs.

title: A predictive model for WHO/ISUP pathologic grading of renal clear cell carcinoma based on CT radiomics: a multicenter study.
rationale_c1: Surgical ccRCC cases from four hospitals remain a retrospective operated cohort with exclusions for small tumors and artifacts.
rationale_c2: Cortical-phase CT radiomics and clinical-imaging factors were used to predict WHO/ISUP grade from surgical pathology.
rationale_c3: Pathological grade was required for inclusion and was available for the 169 analyzed patients.
rationale_c4: Logistic regression retained tumor size, hemorrhage, and tumor thrombus and these entered the combined random-forest model.
rationale_c5: Dual-reader ITK-SNAP segmentation, ICC re-delineation, and nested cross-validation on the United Imaging platform followed the protocol.
probast_rationale: An external cohort is present, but 2264 radiomic features in 169 patients, with few high-grade cases, keep analysis at high risk.
appraisal_note: The external set is 65 patients across three hospitals, and grade III–IV counts are limited.

title: An MRI radiomics model for predicting a prostate-specific antigen response following abiraterone treatment in patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer.
rationale_c1: Sixty mCRPC patients from two hospitals, pooled and randomly split, are a small convenience sample.
rationale_c2: Biparametric MRI radiomics were developed against a PSA response after abiraterone, which matches the stated question.
rationale_c3: The cropped text does not define the PSA-response threshold or show how complete response ascertainment was.
rationale_c4: Cox models are mentioned, but with a validation group of 12 the handling of confounders cannot be judged from the available text.
rationale_c5: Scanner protocols, segmentation, and the feature-to-model procedure are not described in the cropped methods.
probast_rationale: A 48/12 random split of pooled hospitals, a validation AUC confidence interval of 0.564–0.991, and missing methods imply high analysis risk.
appraisal_note: Methods are largely absent from the crop; two hospitals were pooled rather than held out, and two authors are United Imaging employees.

title: An interpretable CT-based deep learning model for predicting overall survival in patients with bladder cancer: a multicenter study.
rationale_c1: The development set is a large retrospective surgical series and one validation arm is TCGA, so population representativeness is uncertain.
rationale_c2: Preoperative CT deep-learning scores were evaluated against overall survival, which is an appropriate prognostic endpoint.
rationale_c3: Median follow-up is reported for the training cohort and three validation cohorts totaling 1456 patients.
rationale_c4: The deep-learning score was combined with independent clinical risk factors from multivariable Cox regression.
rationale_c5: Image acquisition, segmentation, and training hyperparameters are not in the cropped text because the methods section was not captured.
probast_rationale: Three external cohorts are a strength, but TCGA linkage and a high-dimensional CT network still leave analysis at high risk.
appraisal_note: The methods section is missing from the crop; C-indices on the external cohorts were modest (0.62–0.70), including TCGA.

title: An interpretable contrast-enhanced CT radiomics-based pipeline incorporating automatic segmentation for predicting ISUP grade group in ccRCC.
rationale_c1: A single-center retrospective series of 276 operated ccRCC cases is unlikely to represent all patients with renal masses.
rationale_c2: Corticomedullary-phase radiomics from auto-segmented tumors were used to predict ISUP grade group against surgical histology.
rationale_c3: ISUP grade was an inclusion requirement and was available for the training and test patients.
rationale_c4: Radiomics, clinical, and combined models were all built and compared.
rationale_c5: nnU-Net segmentation, fixed preprocessing fit on the training set, and PyRadiomics extraction were described to limit leakage.
probast_rationale: The test set is a random split of one center, and 1197 features were screened across five classifiers.

title: An interpretable machine learning model based on CT imaging for predicting lymphovascular invasion and survival in bladder urothelial carcinoma: a multicenter study.
rationale_c1: Patients came from three retrospective cystectomy centers with exclusions for neoadjuvant therapy and indeterminate lymphovascular invasion.
rationale_c2: Nephrographic-phase CT radiomics and clinical factors were used to predict pathology-defined lymphovascular invasion.
rationale_c3: Lymphovascular-invasion status and disease-free survival follow-up were required, with a reported median follow-up of 25.37 months.
rationale_c4: An SVM radiomics signature was combined with clinical risk factors.
rationale_c5: Blinded dual-reader segmentation, reproducibility filtering, LASSO, and five-fold cross-validation followed the stated workflow.
probast_rationale: A separate testing set reached AUC 0.901, but high-dimensional LASSO features and a higher test-set invasion rate keep analysis at high risk.
appraisal_note: Lymphovascular invasion was less common in the training set (12.5%) than in the testing set (23.2%).

title: An unsupervised learning model that integrates clinical and MRI radiomics features outperforms existing models in predicting the 5-year progression-free survival of prostate cancer patients after prostatectomy: a multicenter study
rationale_c1: From 2238 men at three hospitals, 400 eligible prostatectomy cases remain a selected retrospective cohort.
rationale_c2: Biparametric MRI radiomics plus clinical factors were related to a prespecified five-year progression-free survival definition.
rationale_c3: Progression was recorded in 46% of patients, with median follow-up of 60 months and two external validation groups.
rationale_c4: LASSO-Cox retained five clinical factors and 13 radiomic features before clustering.
rationale_c5: Multicenter MRI parameters, tumor delineation, and the LASSO-Cox plus K-means procedure were applied as described.
probast_rationale: External centers separated risk groups, but cluster names were assigned from observed progression, which inflates apparent performance.
appraisal_note: Research Square preprint; clusters were labeled from observed progression-free survival rather than a locked discrimination metric.

title: Biparametric MRI-based radiomics for prediction of clinically significant prostate cancer of PI-RADS category 3 lesions.
rationale_c1: A single-hospital retrospective series limited to PI-RADS 3 lesions is a narrow convenience sample.
rationale_c2: T2 and DWI radiomics plus PSA density were compared with fusion-biopsy Gleason results.
rationale_c3: Biopsy histology was obtained for the 233 included patients within four weeks of MRI.
rationale_c4: The final model combined the radiomics signature with PSA density and was tested against each component.
rationale_c5: PI-RADS scoring was blinded to pathology, and LASSO with 10-fold cross-validation was used on the training set.
probast_rationale: Validation is a random internal split, and 34 radiomic features were selected in 160 training patients.

title: CT Urography-Based Radiomics to Predict ISUP Grading of Clear Cell Renal Cell Carcinoma.
rationale_c1: The hospital cohort is a retrospective operated series and the external arm is a public TCGA sample, so representativeness is uncertain.
rationale_c2: CT urography radiomics were used to classify ISUP low versus high grade against pathological grade.
rationale_c3: ISUP grade was known for the 328 hospital patients and the 175 TCGA patients included in analysis.
rationale_c4: Logistic regression, MLP, SVM, and XGBoost were fit to radiomic features without a clinical confounder model.
rationale_c5: Two radiologists segmented lesions blinded to clinical data, with a third reader resolving disagreements, before PyRadiomics extraction.
probast_rationale: TCGA external AUCs were lower than training, XGBoost training AUC was 0.96, and four algorithms were screened on 1218 features.
appraisal_note: TCGA is a public external cohort and its stage mix differs from the hospital series, with more pT3 disease.

title: Clinical-radiomics hybrid modeling outperforms conventional models: machine learning enhances stratification of adverse prognostic features in prostate cancer.
rationale_c1: One hundred thirty-seven prostatectomy patients from one hospital are a retrospective convenience sample.
rationale_c2: ADC and T2WI radiomics plus biopsy Gleason, PSA, and prostate volume were used to predict adverse pathology.
rationale_c3: Adverse pathological features from prostatectomy were available under the inclusion rules for all 137 men.
rationale_c4: The selected radiomics model was combined with three clinical variables in a hybrid model.
rationale_c5: ComBat harmonization, dual-reader ROIs with Dice 0.82, and LASSO across five algorithms followed the stated protocol.
probast_rationale: The validation set is a random 95/42 split, and five algorithms were compared on a small single-center cohort.

title: Computed tomography-based radiomics predicts prognostic and treatment-related levels of immune infiltration in the immune microenvironment of clear cell renal cell carcinoma.
rationale_c1: TCGA-KIRC is a public convenience cohort and is not a population sample of ccRCC.
rationale_c2: Plain CT radiomics were aimed at ssGSEA immune groups, but how imaging cases were paired to transcriptomes is incompletely specified.
rationale_c3: Survival analyses dropped cases with follow-up under 30 days, and outcome completeness for the imaged subset is unclear.
rationale_c4: Eight machine-learning classifiers were fit to radiomic features without a clinical confounder adjustment for the imaging model.
rationale_c5: 3D Slicer segmentation, PyRadiomics, Z-score scaling, and correlation filtering were applied as described.
probast_rationale: Labels are computational immune scores, ExtraTrees training AUC was 1.000, and the test AUC fell to 0.753.
appraisal_note: The predicted endpoint is an ssGSEA immune-infiltration proxy on TCGA, not a clinically adjudicated outcome.

title: Development and validation of a radiomics deep learning signature from MRI-guided transrectal ultrasound combined with ultrasound imaging parameters for prostate cancer prediction
rationale_c1: A retrospective two-hospital series of men imaged for suspected prostate cancer remains subject to referral bias.
rationale_c2: MRI-guided ultrasound radiomics and contrast-enhanced ultrasound parameters were used against histopathological prostate cancer status.
rationale_c3: Histopathology was required, and benign versus malignant counts are reported in the training and testing tables.
rationale_c4: The signature integrates imaging radiomics with clinical and contrast-ultrasound parameters.
rationale_c5: PI-RADS reading, MRI-ultrasound fusion, and manual ITK-SNAP segmentation were performed under a described pipeline.
probast_rationale: A second hospital is described as external validation, but the enrolled total is inconsistent and the model is high-dimensional.
appraisal_note: Research Square preprint; methods cite 443 patients while results describe 338.

title: Development of a deep learning system for predicting biochemical recurrence in prostate cancer.
rationale_c1: Biopsy slides from two Tianjin hospitals are a retrospective surgical series, not a population sample.
rationale_c2: Pathologists preferentially selected the five whole-slide images with higher Gleason score, so the image input is tied to a prognostic feature.
rationale_c3: Biochemical recurrence was defined as two PSA values of at least 0.2 ng/mL, with follow-up of 47 to 83 months.
rationale_c4: Patient-level models combined deep-learning pathology features with clinical variables.
rationale_c5: Inception-v3 patch training, color normalization, and multiple-instance learning were applied as described.
probast_rationale: An external hospital test AUC of 0.911 is encouraging, but Gleason-guided slide selection can leak prognosis into the predictors.
appraisal_note: Five slides per patient were chosen with preference for higher Gleason score.

title: Efficacy of PSMA PET/CT radiomics analysis for risk stratification in newly diagnosed prostate cancer: a multicenter study.
rationale_c1: Newly diagnosed prostate cancer cases scanned at four centers are still a retrospective PET-positive convenience sample.
rationale_c2: PSMA PET/CT radiomics were used to separate ISUP grade groups and a PSA threshold of 20 ng/mL.
rationale_c3: Biopsy ISUP grade was an inclusion requirement and baseline PSA was available within two weeks of PET.
rationale_c4: The grade classifiers used radiomic features only, and several algorithms were compared without a locked clinical model.
rationale_c5: PyRadiomics extraction from three segmentations, PCA, and 10-fold cross-validation on two centers were described.
probast_rationale: An external set of 57 patients exists, but 1746 features per segment and multiple classifiers were screened.
appraisal_note: The leading classifier was not the same model in the internal and external sets.

title: Enhancing prediction accuracy for muscle invasion in bladder cancer using a dual-energy CT-based interpretable model incorporating habitat radiomics and deep learning.
rationale_c1: Two hundred surgical bladder cancer cases from one hospital, randomly split, are a retrospective convenience sample.
rationale_c2: Dual-energy CT habitat radiomics and deep learning were used to predict pathology-defined muscle invasion.
rationale_c3: Muscle-invasion status on the pathology report was required for the 200 included patients.
rationale_c4: Effective atomic number from stepwise regression was combined with habitat and ResNet features.
rationale_c5: Readers were blinded to pathology, ICCs were calculated, and transfer-learning networks were trained as specified.
probast_rationale: The test set is an internal 7:3 split, and training AUC 0.981 fell to 0.833.
appraisal_note: There is no external center; the training AUC of 0.981 dropped to 0.833 on the internal test split.

title: Evaluating the prognostic value of radiomics and clinical features in metastatic prostate cancer using [<sup>68</sup>Ga]Ga-PSMA-11 PET/CT.
rationale_c1: Men with biochemically recurrent prostate cancer imaged at two Perth hospitals were selected for oligometastatic or imaging-negative disease.
rationale_c2: PSMA PET radiomics and clinical features were modeled against overall survival with Cox regression.
rationale_c3: Overall survival was analyzed in the 180 patients who had metastases after prespecified exclusions from 238 enrolled men.
rationale_c4: Clinical-only, radiomics-only, and combined LASSO-Cox models were compared with optimism correction.
rationale_c5: Semi-automatic lesion segmentation and radiomic extraction on accredited scanners followed the described pipeline.
probast_rationale: Optimism-corrected C-indices are reported, but 13 models were built from 118 features without a held-out external test.
appraisal_note: Both hospitals were pooled and evaluated with bootstrap optimism correction rather than a center-held-out test.

title: Evaluation of a PSA and transrectal prostate ultrasound video-based machine learning model as a tool for prostate cancer diagnosis.
rationale_c1: A single-center retrospective series of 928 men referred for prostate ultrasound is a convenience sample.
rationale_c2: Transrectal ultrasound video radiomics plus PSA and clinical measures were compared with transperineal biopsy histology.
rationale_c3: Histopathology and preoperative PSA were inclusion requirements for the training and test cohorts.
rationale_c4: Six algorithms combined ultrasound features with PSA, prostate volume, and age, and SHAP ranked those clinical inputs.
rationale_c5: A standardized transrectal acquisition protocol and video-volume radiomics extraction were applied as described.
probast_rationale: The test set is a random internal split, and six algorithms were screened on the same center.

title: Fully automated segmentation and classification of renal tumors on CT scans via machine learning.
rationale_c1: The source is a consecutive nephrectomy registry, but only three RCC subtypes plus angiomyolipoma were retained, so the spectrum is restricted.
rationale_c2: Automated CT segmentation and radiomic plus Hounsfield-unit features were used to classify pathological tumor subtype.
rationale_c3: Subtype labels came from surgical pathology for the 561 included masses.
rationale_c4: Random-forest models combined radiomic features with conventional radiological measurements and were stratified by tumor size.
rationale_c5: A 3D U-Net and a five-fold split that preserved subtype mix were trained as described.
probast_rationale: Evaluation is five-fold internal validation at one center, with class imbalance and weaker segmentation of masses under 4 cm.
appraisal_note: For tumors smaller than 4 cm, tumor Dice was 0.65 and subtype accuracy was 0.68.

title: Integration of multi-scale radiomics and deep learning for Ki-67 prediction in clear cell renal carcinoma.
rationale_c1: All 627 ccRCC cases came from three hospitals in one province, so geographic representativeness is limited.
rationale_c2: Multiscale CT radiomics, deep-learning features, and clinical variables were used to predict the postoperative Ki-67 index.
rationale_c3: A Ki-67 index on the pathology report was required for every included patient and was read by two pathologists.
rationale_c4: The stacking model fused the best unimodal learners, including clinical features.
rationale_c5: Isotropic resampling, habitat and peritumoral masks, and ICC filtering were applied before external testing.
probast_rationale: External AUC was 0.756, but the 5% Ki-67 cutoff is author-defined and the feature space is large.
appraisal_note: High Ki-67 was defined at a 5% threshold that the authors note is not a universal standard.

title: Interpretable multiparametric MRI radiomics-based machine learning model for preoperative differentiation between benign and malignant prostate masses: a diagnostic, multicenter study.
rationale_c1: Patients imaged for suspected prostate cancer at two hospitals are a retrospective referral cohort.
rationale_c2: T2WI and DWI radiomics were used to separate benign from malignant masses against pathology or a biopsy-based composite reference.
rationale_c3: Diagnostic labels were obtained for all 567 enrolled patients after exclusions for missing MRI or pathology.
rationale_c4: Five machine-learning models were trained on radiomic features without a reported clinical confounder adjustment.
rationale_c5: ITK-SNAP segmentation, PyRadiomics, and LASSO with five-fold cross-validation were applied as described.
probast_rationale: An external test of 63 patients is reported, but 2632 features and a mixed biopsy reference keep outcome and analysis at risk.
appraisal_note: The reference standard mixed prostatectomy histology with a biopsy and follow-up composite.

title: Intratumoral and peritumoral radiomics using multi-phase contrast-enhanced CT for diagnosis of renal oncocytoma and chromophobe renal cell carcinoma: a multicenter retrospective study.
rationale_c1: Ninety-two oncocytoma and chromophobe RCC cases pooled from five centers are a small, highly selected surgical sample.
rationale_c2: Intratumoral and peritumoral CT radiomics were compared with histopathological and immunohistochemical diagnosis.
rationale_c3: Pathology and immunohistochemistry were required for the 65 training and 27 validation cases.
rationale_c4: SVM models used radiomic features only, without clinical confounder adjustment.
rationale_c5: Radiologist and software segmentations, ICC filtering above 0.75, and LASSO feature selection were performed as described.
probast_rationale: Centers were pooled into a 7:3 split of 92 patients, and validation AUC ranged from 0.60 to 0.90.
appraisal_note: Five centers were pooled rather than held out, and one validation model AUC was 0.60.

title: Machine learning models for discriminating clinically significant from clinically insignificant prostate cancer using bi-parametric magnetic resonance imaging
rationale_c1: After exclusions, 77 lesions from one hospital remain a small retrospective convenience sample.
rationale_c2: T2-weighted and ADC radiomics were used to separate clinically significant from insignificant cancer on fusion biopsy.
rationale_c3: Histopathology was available for the 47 clinically significant and 30 insignificant lesions that remained.
rationale_c4: Logistic regression and SVM models used radiomic features only, without clinical confounders.
rationale_c5: Dual-reader segmentation, correlation filtering, and a train-test split performed before augmentation followed the protocol.
probast_rationale: The test set is an internal split of 77 lesions, with class imbalance and high-dimensional radiomics.
appraisal_note: Only 77 lesions remained, and the authors note that augmentation would make much of the sample synthetic.

title: Machine learning-based radiomics for bladder cancer staging: evaluating the role of imaging timing in differentiating T2 from T3 disease.
rationale_c1: Single-center retrospective series of 97 cystectomy patients after exclusions for small or poorly seen tumors, so representativeness of the broader bladder-cancer staging population is uncertain.
rationale_c2: Contrast-enhanced CT radiomics and radical-cystectomy pathologic stage are appropriate measures for distinguishing intravesical from extravesical disease.
rationale_c3: Patients with incomplete clinical or imaging data were excluded, and the analyzed cohort has histopathologic stage for the classification endpoint.
rationale_c4: A combined model adds preoperative clinical variables, including creatinine, hemoglobin, and comorbidity factors, to the radiomic features.
rationale_c5: Contrast-enhanced CT was acquired under routine staging protocols and features were extracted with IBSI-compliant software by experienced readers.
probast_rationale: Random-forest staging model with five-fold cross-validation only in 97 patients, and the abstract and results disagree on whether cohort 1 is the early post-TURB subset or the whole sample.
appraisal_note: Cohort definitions by TURB-to-CT interval conflict between the abstract and the results, and discrimination is reported only from five-fold cross-validation.

title: Machine learning-based radiomics from multiparametric MRI for predicting aggressive pathology in clear cell renal cell carcinoma.
rationale_c1: Cases were pooled from two hospitals and TCIA rather than drawn as a population sample, and only 43 tumors were aggressive.
rationale_c2: Multiparametric MRI radiomics with segmentation blinded to pathology, and WHO/ISUP grade plus stage, appropriately define aggressive versus indolent ccRCC.
rationale_c3: Inclusion required complete clinical, pathologic, and imaging data, and incomplete examinations were excluded.
rationale_c4: The classifiers do not adjust for tumor size or other clinical covariates even though aggressive tumors were much larger and the top features were shape descriptors.
rationale_c5: Images were resampled, co-registered, and z-score normalized before feature extraction, and segmentations were reviewed by a senior radiologist.
probast_rationale: More than 5,000 classifier–feature combinations were screened with SMOTE and five-fold cross-validation on pooled centers, including TCIA, without a held-out external test.
appraisal_note: The leading T2WI features are shape metrics and aggressive tumors were far larger, so the AUC near 0.96 may largely reflect size rather than texture.

title: Multi-channel multiphase CT-based deep learning and radiomics fusion model for noninvasive pathological grading of clear cell renal cell carcinoma.
rationale_c1: All 496 patients came from one institution and were randomly split, so referral and scanner patterns may not represent other ccRCC populations.
rationale_c2: Triphasic CT, radiomics, and ResNet50 features were paired with WHO/ISUP grade, and readers assessing semantic imaging signs were blinded to pathology.
rationale_c3: Enrollment required complete clinical and pathologic documentation, and cases with incomplete records were excluded.
rationale_c4: Univariate and multivariate analyses identified age as associated with grade, and the final model combined clinical variables with imaging features.
rationale_c5: CT scanners, phase timing, resampling, and windowing were specified and applied before segmentation and training.
probast_rationale: The 70/30 test set is a random split of a single institution, the split was not stratified, and deep-learning plus radiomic features were tuned on the same pool.

title: Multicenter study demonstrates unsupervised learning derived from magnetic resonance images identify prognosis in prostate cancer patients after prostatectomy
rationale_c1: Three hospitals contributed center-held-out cohorts, but 2,238 records were reduced to 400 eligible patients and the authors cite retrospective selection bias.
rationale_c2: Preoperative MRI radiomics plus clinical factors are appropriate predictors of progression-free survival defined by biochemical recurrence or imaging-detected metastasis.
rationale_c3: Median follow-up was 60 months, progression occurred in 46% of patients, and center-specific event counts are reported.
rationale_c4: LASSO-Cox selected clinical and radiomic features into a radiomic-clinical model that was compared with EAU, CAPRA, and PIPEN scores.
rationale_c5: MRI acquisition parameters are not described in the cropped text, and the authors note that contrast-enhanced images were not segmented.
probast_rationale: External C-indices are reported at two other centers, but radiomic feature handling is thinly described and the external sets are small.
appraisal_note: This is a Research Square preprint, and the cropped text does not describe MRI acquisition or the segmentation protocol.

title: Multimodal deep learning framework integrating multiphase CT and histopathological whole slide imaging for predicting recurrence in ccRCC.
rationale_c1: All 274 patients were identified from one hospital pathology database and then randomly split, so the sample is a single-center convenience cohort.
rationale_c2: Multiphase CT and whole-slide images, with recurrence or metastasis versus non-recurrence after at least three years, match the prognostic question.
rationale_c3: Missing or contaminated slides and incomplete imaging were exclusion criteria, and a minimum three-year follow-up was required.
rationale_c4: The fusion networks compare imaging modalities but do not adjust for stage, grade, or other clinicopathologic confounders of recurrence.
rationale_c5: CT and slide-scanning procedures, ROI construction, and the training–test split are described and were applied to the cohort.
probast_rationale: Several deep-fusion variants were compared on a random 6:4 split of one hospital, and the authors state that external validation is still pending.
appraisal_note: The test cohort is a random split of a single hospital, and the authors explicitly defer external validation.

title: Multimodal fusion radiomic-immunologic scoring model: accurate identification of prostate cancer progression.
rationale_c1: This is a single-center retrospective series of 157 men, so representativeness beyond that hospital is uncertain.
rationale_c2: mpMRI radiomics and CD3/CD8 immunohistochemistry are appropriate inputs for the stated progression endpoints, which are defined with standard BCR, CRPC, and metastasis criteria.
rationale_c3: Median follow-up was 36 months and patients were classified by documented progression status at the study end.
rationale_c4: Progression and non-progression groups differed in Gleason score, PSA, and T stage, and those factors were not entered as covariates in the radiomic-immunologic score.
rationale_c5: Imaging, immunohistochemistry, and the multi-step feature-selection workflow are described as a standardized institutional pipeline.
probast_rationale: SMOTE expanded 157 patients to 200 before 10-fold cross-validation, which can leak between folds in a single-center radiomic model.
appraisal_note: SMOTE increased the analytic cohort from 157 to 200 patients before cross-validation, which risks optimistic AUC estimates.

title: Radiogenomic correlation of hypoxia-related biomarkers in clear cell renal cell carcinoma.
rationale_c1: The sample is a TCGA-KIRC/TCIA subset of 190 mostly White men, which the authors note limits generalizability.
rationale_c2: CT radiomics and median-split expression of prespecified hypoxia genes are appropriate measures for a radiogenomic classification aim.
rationale_c3: Analysis was restricted to cases with matched CT and complete expression data, and cohort characteristics are tabulated.
rationale_c4: The random-forest model does not adjust for stage, grade, or other clinical factors, and there is no external cohort.
rationale_c5: The authors intentionally skipped intensity normalization on multi-scanner TCIA images, so whether features were measured as intended across scanners is unclear.
probast_rationale: A high-dimensional random forest predicted median-split gene expression in one public cohort without external validation or a reported discrimination metric.
appraisal_note: The modeled endpoint is median-split hypoxia-gene expression, and the cropped text describes performance only qualitatively.

title: Reproducibility of MRI-derived radiomic features in prostate cancer detection: a methodological approach.
rationale_c1: Images were randomly taken from the public Prostate158 set as 41 cancers versus 41 healthy controls, which is not a clinical referral population.
rationale_c2: T2-weighted and ADC radiomic features are appropriate inputs for an image-based cancer-versus-noncancer classification.
rationale_c3: Label provenance, exclusions, and completeness of the public cases are not described beyond the 82 selected examinations.
rationale_c4: No clinical covariates were available or adjusted for, and healthy controls do not share the confounding structure of men undergoing biopsy.
rationale_c5: Feature extraction with SERA, ICC filtering, and the dimensionality-reduction and classifier workflow are described and applied.
probast_rationale: Ten classifiers and seven dimensionality-reduction methods were searched in 82 public cases, with AUC up to 0.93 and no external clinical cohort.
appraisal_note: Classifying cancer against healthy controls from Prostate158 has high applicability concern for biopsy decisions in men with suspected prostate cancer.

title: Subregion-based radiomics analysis for predicting the histological grade of clear cell renal cell carcinoma.
rationale_c1: Development used TCIA cases, a public convenience sample, with only 65 local patients for external testing.
rationale_c2: CT subregion radiomics, delineated blinded to grade, are appropriate for predicting histologic grade.
rationale_c3: Training, internal-test, and external-set grade counts are reported, and low-reproducibility features were removed by ICC.
rationale_c4: Logistic and support-vector models use three radiomic features without adjustment for tumor size or other clinicopathologic confounders.
rationale_c5: Manual segmentation, ICC filtering, Gaussian-mixture subregions, and LASSO selection are described and were applied, despite residual scanner differences.
probast_rationale: External AUCs are about 0.74–0.77 in 65 local patients after TCIA development, with multiple machine-learning models and a small event count in the external high-grade group.

title: The interpretable CT-based vision transformer model for preoperative prediction of clear cell renal cell carcinoma SSIGN score and outcome.
rationale_c1: Eight hundred forty-five patients from multiple hospitals were enrolled with stated inclusion and exclusion criteria, and 253 patients from separate hospitals formed the test cohort.
rationale_c2: Cortical-medullary and parenchymal-phase CT vision-transformer features are appropriate predictors of the pathologic SSIGN score and of progression-free survival.
rationale_c3: Complete clinical and pathologic data were required, and baseline characteristics are reported for the training and test cohorts.
rationale_c4: The vision-transformer models use imaging features alone and do not adjust for clinicopathologic covariates when classifying SSIGN risk.
rationale_c5: Contrast timing, inclusion image-quality thresholds, and multicenter preprocessing before feature extraction are described and applied.
probast_rationale: A separate-hospital test set supports transportability, but 768 vision-transformer features per phase were mined without a prespecified model.

title: The predictive value of radiomics and deep learning for synchronous distant metastasis in clear cell renal cell carcinoma.
rationale_c1: Non-metastatic controls were randomly sampled to match metastatic tumor size, so the two-hospital series is an enriched case-control sample rather than a consecutive cohort.
rationale_c2: Preoperative contrast CT radiomics and deep-learning features are appropriate for pathology-confirmed synchronous distant metastasis.
rationale_c3: Training (143) and validation (62) counts with metastasis status are reported, and poor-quality scans were excluded.
rationale_c4: The fused radiomics and ResNet model does not show adjustment for stage or other clinical confounders of metastasis.
rationale_c5: CT was obtained within two weeks of diagnosis, tumors were segmented in ITK-SNAP, and features were extracted with a stated toolkit.
probast_rationale: Multiple machine-learning and deep-learning architectures were compared, the validation hospital has only 19 metastatic cases, and controls were size-matched.
appraisal_note: Controls without metastasis were randomly sampled to match tumor size, which distorts the clinical prevalence of synchronous metastasis.

title: The role of endothelial cell-related gene COL1A1 in prostate cancer diagnosis and immunotherapy: insights from machine learning and single-cell analysis.
rationale_c1: Training uses TCGA-PRAD tumor and normal samples, a public convenience set rather than a screening or biopsy population.
rationale_c2: Endothelial-cell gene expression is an appropriate input for a transcriptomic classifier of prostate adenocarcinoma versus normal tissue.
rationale_c3: TCGA and four GEO cohorts are named with tumor and normal sample counts.
rationale_c4: One hundred eight algorithm configurations were screened without adjustment for clinical confounders of diagnosis or prognosis.
rationale_c5: The single-cell, clustering, and machine-learning pipeline is described and applied to the stated public cohorts.
probast_rationale: A diagnostic signature was fit on TCGA and checked in four GEO sets, but the cropped text does not report AUC or calibration and the algorithm search was very large.
appraisal_note: External GEO cohorts are named, but discrimination metrics are not present in the cropped text.

title: Unsupervised learning-based quantitative analysis of CT intratumoral subregions predicts risk stratification of bladder cancer patients.
rationale_c1: The study enrolled 1,017 histologically confirmed patients from two centers, with center B held out as an external validation cohort of 239.
rationale_c2: Venous-phase CT subregion radiomics are appropriate predictors of muscle invasion and AJCC stage confirmed after resection.
rationale_c3: Center-specific sample sizes, muscle-invasive counts, and stage distributions are reported for training and external validation.
rationale_c4: A clinicopathologic model was built with stepwise regression and fused with the radiomic subregion models.
rationale_c5: The cropped methods section is empty, so segmentation reproducibility and CT acquisition parameters cannot be confirmed.
probast_rationale: External AUROCs are reported, but seven radiomic models were developed and the cropped text omits the segmentation and acquisition protocol.
appraisal_note: The cropped file has no methods narrative, so predictor measurement was judged from the abstract, results, and limitations only.

title: A perioperative multi-modal fusion and deep learning-based prognostic system for upper tract urothelial carcinoma: a multi-institutional study.
rationale_c1: Six hundred twenty-three patients from six institutions met stated inclusion and exclusion criteria, with 150 patients from four other centers held out for external validation.
rationale_c2: Preoperative CT urography radiomics and deep-learning features plus postoperative pathology are appropriate for post-nephroureterectomy risk stratification.
rationale_c3: Patients lacking complete clinicopathologic or follow-up data were excluded, and C-indexes are reported in training, internal, and external sets.
rationale_c4: A clinical model was fit and its prognostic score was fused with radiomic and deep-learning scores in the combined nomogram.
rationale_c5: The study follows the CLEAR checklist, and CT urography segmentation with PyRadiomics extraction is described as applied.
probast_rationale: External validation is genuine, but high-dimensional radiomic and deep-learning features were still selected inside the development centers.
appraisal_note: Predictors include postoperative pathologic stage because the intended use is immediately after nephroureterectomy, not preoperative counseling.

title: CT-based radiogenomic prediction of ICAM1 and RAET1E as biomarkers of NK cytotoxicity in clear cell renal cell carcinoma.
rationale_c1: Imaging-expression correlation used 143 TCGA-KIRC cases with CT, a selected public subset, plus a 26-patient immunohistochemistry set.
rationale_c2: PyRadiomics features from segmented CT volumes are appropriate predictors of high versus low ICAM1 and RAET1E expression.
rationale_c3: Matched imaging-expression cases and the 26-case immunohistochemistry validation counts are reported.
rationale_c4: The L1-SVM does not adjust for stage, grade, or other clinical confounders of gene expression.
rationale_c5: Manual 3D segmentation checked by two radiologists and the feature-filtering steps are described and applied.
probast_rationale: Leave-one-out selection among thousands of radiomic features on a public subset, with external immunohistochemistry in only 26 cases, leaves a high overfitting risk.
appraisal_note: The predicted targets are ICAM1 and RAET1E expression, and external immunohistochemistry includes only 26 tumors.

title: Combined radiomics, PI-RADS, and clinical model improve significant prostate cancer prediction and guide biopsy decision.
rationale_c1: Men were consecutively enrolled at a single hospital and randomly split, so the cohort may reflect local referral practice.
rationale_c2: Gland radiomics, PI-RADS, and clinical variables are appropriate predictors of biopsy-defined significant prostate cancer (grade group 2 or higher).
rationale_c3: Cases missing MRI, clinical variables, or biopsy results were excluded, and cohort characteristics are tabulated by split.
rationale_c4: The best model combines PI-RADS, radiomics, and clinical variables, so major diagnostic covariates are included.
rationale_c5: bpMRI or mpMRI acquisition, automatic gland segmentation, and the STARD and CLAIM workflow are described and applied.
probast_rationale: Discrimination is estimated on a random 20% split of one center after comparing several machine-learning models on handcrafted radiomic features.

title: Deep learning models built from PSMA PET of the primary tumor can predict synchronous and metachronous prostate cancer metastases.
rationale_c1: Ninety-four treatment-naive patients from one veterans hospital form a small convenience series.
rationale_c2: Synchronous metastasis labels were read from the same PSMA PET used to build the prostate input, so outcome measurement is not clearly independent of the predictors.
rationale_c3: Non-metastatic patients needed 33 months of follow-up, but metachronous event counts and losses are not fully reported in the cropped text.
rationale_c4: The cropped text does not show a prespecified clinical adjustment set for the convolutional or multimodal model.
rationale_c5: PSMA PET used standardized acquisition, aPROMISE prostate segmentation, and a stated training schedule.
probast_rationale: Models were trained on 94 scans with an acknowledged overfitting risk, and no independent test cohort is described.
appraisal_note: Synchronous metastasis was labeled on the same PSMA PET that supplied the primary-tumor input, in a 94-patient single-institution series.

title: Developing an interpretable clinical-radiomics machine learning model using whole transition zone MRI analysis for improving diagnosis of transition zone prostate cancer.
rationale_c1: Two hundred eighty pathologically confirmed cases from two institutions were enrolled with stated criteria, and center B (n=77) was an external test set.
rationale_c2: Whole-transition-zone T2-weighted and ADC radiomics plus clinical variables are appropriate for distinguishing transition-zone cancer from benign hyperplasia on surgical pathology.
rationale_c3: Incomplete MRI or clinical data were excluded, and cancer and hyperplasia counts are given for training, internal, and external sets.
rationale_c4: Independent clinical variables, including PI-RADS and PSA, were combined with the radiomic model.
rationale_c5: Center-specific 1.5T and 3.0T biparametric MRI protocols, segmentation, and feature extraction are described and applied.
probast_rationale: Six algorithms were compared on more than a thousand radiomic features, and the clinical-radiomics AUC fell from 0.963 in training to 0.829 externally.
appraisal_note: Training AUC of 0.963 dropped to 0.829 in the external center, which suggests residual optimism after multi-algorithm screening.

title: Integrating single-cell analysis and machine learning algorithms to explore lactylation-related molecular mechanisms and therapeutic responses in clear cell renal cell carcinoma and identifying CDT1 as a potential biomarker.
rationale_c1: The training set is TCGA-KIRC after dropping incomplete records, a public convenience cohort.
rationale_c2: Lactylation-related transcriptomic features are appropriate inputs for a survival model in ccRCC.
rationale_c3: External clinical annotation was incomplete, and the authors could not compare baseline covariates across TCGA, E-MTAB-1980, and GSE29609.
rationale_c4: One hundred one algorithm combinations were screened, and unmeasured confounders are cited as a reason the GSE29609 risk split failed.
rationale_c5: The single-cell, WGCNA, and multi-algorithm survival pipeline is described and applied to the named cohorts.
probast_rationale: External C-indexes are reported, but a large algorithm search on TCGA did not reproduce risk separation in GSE29609.
appraisal_note: Risk groups did not separate in GSE29609, and the authors report that clinical covariates could not be aligned across cohorts.

title: Multimodal deep learning for prediction of postoperative recurrence in clear cell renal cell carcinoma: a clinical-radiologic-pathologic approach.
rationale_c1: Two hundred seventy consecutive patients from three hospitals were enrolled, with 215 used for development and 55 held out as an independent test cohort whose size matches the third hospital.
rationale_c2: Clinical, CT, and histopathology features are appropriate predictors of recurrence within five years after nephrectomy.
rationale_c3: Missing multimodal data were handled by complete-case exclusion, and recurrence counts are reported.
rationale_c4: Fusion models combine predicted probabilities from clinical and imaging modalities rather than imaging alone.
rationale_c5: CT acquisition parameters and segmentation procedures are not described in the cropped text.
probast_rationale: Twenty-five classifiers were built, and an independent-test AUROC of 0.967 is unusually high for five-year recurrence.
appraisal_note: An independent-test AUROC of 0.967 is unusually high, and the cropped text does not fully document the imaging protocol.

title: Multiphase CT-Based Tumor and Peritumoral Radiomics for Characterization of Clear Cell Renal Cell Carcinoma.
rationale_c1: Two hundred fifty patients from affiliate hospitals of one university were analyzed retrospectively without an external cohort.
rationale_c2: Four-phase CT radiomics from tumor and peritumoral rims are appropriate predictors of pathologic stage, grade, and aggressiveness.
rationale_c3: Cases missing any CT phase or outcome data were excluded, and class imbalance is described.
rationale_c4: Elastic-net and random-forest models use radiomic features only, without clinicopathologic covariates.
rationale_c5: The authors state that scanner heterogeneity was not addressed, so consistent feature measurement across scanners is uncertain.
probast_rationale: Ten-fold cross-validation of 1,874 features per region produced an aggressiveness AUC of 0.915 without external testing.
appraisal_note: There is no external test set, and the aggressiveness AUC of 0.915 comes from internal cross-validation only.

title: Predicting Response to Neoadjuvant Hormonal Therapy and Prognostic Outcomes in High-Risk Prostate Cancer Using MRI-Based Radiomics
rationale_c1: One hundred forty men were treated at a single center and split internally, so representativeness is uncertain.
rationale_c2: Pre-treatment mpMRI radiomics are appropriate predictors of pathologic response after neoadjuvant hormonal therapy and prostatectomy.
rationale_c3: The cropped text reports a complete clinicopathologic cohort with a 98/42 stratified internal split and response counts.
rationale_c4: Clinical and MRI differences are tabulated, but the cropped results end before the multivariable model specification.
rationale_c5: Eligibility, mpMRI timing before hormonal therapy, and reproducibility filtering of features are described.
probast_rationale: The design is a single-center internal split of an MRI radiomics response model, and discrimination metrics are absent from the cropped text.
appraisal_note: Research Square preprint of the same Huadong Hospital series as REC-AIBIOGU-001023; model metrics are not in this crop.

title: Predicting response to neoadjuvant hormonal therapy and prognostic outcomes in high-risk prostate cancer using MRI-based radiomics.
rationale_c1: All 140 patients were treated at one hospital and divided into an internal training and validation split.
rationale_c2: Cribriform histology from the prostatectomy specimen is used beside imaging to predict complete response defined on that same specimen, so measurement independence is unclear.
rationale_c3: Training (n=98) and internal validation (n=42) cohorts with complete clinicopathologic data are described.
rationale_c4: Including post-prostatectomy cribriform histology does not constitute proper preoperative confounder control for response prediction.
rationale_c5: mpMRI before neoadjuvant therapy, feature selection, and classifier training are described for the single-center protocol.
probast_rationale: Internal validation AUC reached 0.979 after multiple classifiers, with no external cohort and a pathologic feature taken from the outcome specimen.
appraisal_note: Internal-validation AUC of 0.979 is implausibly high, cribriform histology may leak from the prostatectomy specimen, and this is the published twin of REC-AIBIOGU-001020.

title: Radiomics-based interpretable machine learning model from multiphasic CT imaging for predicting pathological grade in upper tract urothelial carcinoma: a multicenter study.
rationale_c1: Three hundred thirty-eight patients from three hospitals met stated criteria, with centers 2 and 3 (n=102) held out as the test set.
rationale_c2: Multiphasic CT urography radiomics are appropriate predictors of WHO pathologic grade after nephroureterectomy.
rationale_c3: Incomplete clinical, pathologic, or imaging data were excluded, and training and test counts are reported.
rationale_c4: Six imaging-only algorithms were compared, without a clinicopathologic covariate adjustment in the grade model.
rationale_c5: CT urography timing, PyRadiomics extraction, ICC filtering, and LASSO selection are described and applied.
probast_rationale: LightGBM training AUC was 0.945 versus 0.829 in the external centers after screening six algorithms on 3,864 features.

title: Radiomics-based tumor heterogeneity augments clinicopathological models for predicting recurrence in high-risk clear cell renal cell carcinoma after nephrectomy.
rationale_c1: One hundred ninety-four high-risk ccRCC patients from three hospitals met S-TRAC-adapted criteria, with an external test set of 47.
rationale_c2: Corticomedullary-phase CT radiomics are appropriate predictors of recurrence-free survival confirmed by imaging or pathology.
rationale_c3: Incomplete clinicopathologic or follow-up data were excluded, and recurrence occurred in 62 patients.
rationale_c4: The radiomic random-survival-forest score was compared and combined with the Leibovich clinicopathologic score.
rationale_c5: Preoperative CT timing, segmentation, and PyRadiomics extraction on the corticomedullary phase are described and applied.
probast_rationale: Time-dependent AUCs were estimated in an external set of only 47 patients after radiomic survival-forest feature selection, with a clear drop from training.
appraisal_note: The external test set has 47 patients, so the time-dependent AUC confidence intervals are wide.

title: Urinary volatilomics using liquid-liquid extraction and gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (GC-MS) combined with machine learning algorithms as a tool for diagnosis and surveillance of urothelial bladder cancer.
rationale_c1: One hundred clinic attendees were split into 50 cancer cases and 50 controls that mix never-cancer and remission samples, not a consecutive diagnostic series.
rationale_c2: Urine GC-MS volatilomic features are appropriate candidate predictors of cystoscopy-evaluated bladder cancer.
rationale_c3: All 100 collected urine samples were analyzed, and comorbidity counts in both groups are described.
rationale_c4: Comorbidities were more common in controls and were not adjusted for in the metabolite classifiers.
rationale_c5: Solvent extraction, GC-MS, and the machine-learning workflow are described and applied to the biobanked aliquots.
probast_rationale: Five algorithms with recursive feature elimination were evaluated by repeated five-fold cross-validation in 100 samples and no external set.
appraisal_note: Controls combine people who never had bladder cancer with patients in remission, and comorbidities were unbalanced.

title: Connecting Histopathology Imaging and Proteomics in Kidney Cancer through Machine Learning.
rationale_c1: CPTAC ccRCC is a convenience public cohort, not a population sample.
rationale_c2: Proteomics and histology are matched to the tumor-versus-normal question.
rationale_c3: 194 samples with 9964 proteins are described, including 110 tumors and 84 normal kidneys.
rationale_c4: Performance is 10-fold cross-validation on the same CPTAC set, with no external cohort.
rationale_c5: Random-forest and CNN procedures are described.
probast_rationale: Public CPTAC cohort and internal cross-validation only; the endpoint is tumor versus normal.
appraisal_note: Diagnostic performance is for tumor versus normal tissue, which is a narrow reading of biomarker discovery.

title: A Critical Analysis of the Robustness of Radiomics to Variations in Segmentation Methods in 18F-PSMA-1007 PET Images of Prostate Cancer.
rationale_c1: Single-center consecutive PET cohort, not a population sample.
rationale_c2: PSMA-PET radiomics are appropriate to the risk-separation question.
rationale_c3: Only 78 patients (43 low risk, 35 high risk).
rationale_c4: No external cohort; the study is primarily a segmentation-robustness analysis.
rationale_c5: Segmentation methods, feature extraction, and classifiers are described.
probast_rationale: Small single-center sample and no external validation. Risk labels need the full risk definition.
appraisal_note: The paper's main aim is segmentation robustness. The risk-classifier AUC is a secondary result.

title: A disease-centric vision-language foundation model for precision oncology in kidney cancer.
rationale_c1: Large multi-center CT collection, still not a population-based sample.
rationale_c2: CT tasks cover anatomy, diagnosis, and survival.
rationale_c3: Pretraining used 6867 patients and evaluation used 1942 patients across centers.
rationale_c4: External multi-center and TCIA cohorts are held out from fine-tuning.
rationale_c5: Two-stage pretraining and downstream tasks are described.
probast_rationale: External centers are a strength. Participants remain a convenience imaging cohort, and the foundation-model analysis is complex.
appraisal_note: The deliverable is a foundation model rather than a named biomarker signature.
